<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
For every nonzero effective curve class \(\beta\in H_2(X,\mathbb Z)\),
\[
 C_{2,\beta}=\hbar Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}},
 \qquad
 Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}}\in \text{St}_{\rm cyc}(X/\mathbb A).
\]
More explicitly, there are finitely many Steinberg subvarieties
\(L_{\beta,j}\subset X\times_\mathbb A X\) and rational numbers \(c_{\beta,j}\in{\mathbb Q}\) such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Zbeta-Steinberg}
 Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}} = \sum_j c_{\beta,j}[L_{\beta,j}]_T .
\end{equation}

Moreover, for every divisor \(D\) equipped with an equivariant lift
\(D_T\), the quantum product with $D$ is given by 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:divisor-main}
 M_D
 =
 D_T\cup
 +
 \hbar
 \sum_{\beta>0}
 (D\cdot\beta)q^\beta\mathbf{F}_{2,\beta},
\end{equation}
where $\mathbf{F}_{2,\beta}$ is the correspondence 
$$
\mathbf{F}_{2,\beta}: H_T^*(X)_{\mathrm{loc}}\to H_T^*(X)_{\mathrm{loc}}
$$
defined by 
$$
\mathbf{F}_{2,\beta}(\delta)=\operatorname{PD}_X^{-1}p_{2*}\bigl(p_1^*\delta\cap\mathop{\rm cl}\nolimits_T^{\mathrm{BM}}(Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}})\bigr).$$
Here $p_i: X\times X\to X$ are projections for $i=1,2$.

                                                                                               
Let $\Theta$ be the theta class of $X$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:theta-main}
 \frac{M_\Theta-\Theta_T\cup}{\hbar}
 =
 \sum_{\beta>0}
 (\Theta\cdot\beta)q^\beta \mathbf{F}_{2,\beta}
 \in \operatorname{Act}\!\left(\widehat{\text{St}}_{\rm cyc}(X/\mathbb A)\right).
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{cor_theta_square}
For $\beta\ne0$, define the one-pointed reduced evaluation class in localized cohomology by
\[
 Z_{1,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}}
 :=\operatorname{PD}_X^{-1}\operatorname{ev}_*[\overline M_{0,1}(X,\beta)]^{\mathrm{red}}_T.
\]
Applying the ordinary divisor equation twice, and using the standard/reduced identity, gives
\[
 \Theta_T\star\Theta_T=\Theta_T^2+
 \hbar\sum_{\beta>0}(\Theta\cdot\beta)^2q^\beta Z_{1,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}}.
\]
                                                                                                                            

In \cite{JKT}, the following formula will be calculated in rank two case. Let $E_4(q)=1+240\sum_{n\ge1}\sigma_3(n)q^n$ and $\sigma_3(n)=\sum_{k\mid n}k^3$, Then we have
\[
 \Theta\star\Theta-\Theta^2=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\frac{\hbar^2}{60}
 \bigl(E_4(q)-1+12(E_4(q^2)-1)\bigr)1_X,&g=2,\\[4pt]
 \displaystyle\frac{g-1}{3}\hbar^2(E_4(q^2)-1)1_X,&g>2.
 \end{cases}
\]
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:intro-character}
The class $Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}$ is symmetric and diagonally $\Gamma$-invariant, and
\[
 Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}=\sum_\kappa Z_{B,\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}},\qquad
 \mathbf F_{Z_{B,\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}}}
   =\mathsf P_\kappa\mathbf F_B\mathsf P_\kappa,\qquad
 (Z_{B,\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}})^{\mathsf t}=Z_{B,\kappa^{-1}}^{\mathrm{red}}.
\]
For $\kappa\ne1$, both contractions with $\Theta_T$ vanish in $E_r$-valued equivariant Chow groups. Individual blocks are symmetric when $\kappa=\kappa^{-1}$, in particular for rank two. For a $\Gamma$-fixed class $\beta$, its positive-degree quantum
coefficient on a character block is
\[
 [q^\beta](M_\Theta)|_\kappa
  =(\Theta\cdot\beta)\hbar\,\mathbf F_{Z_{\{\beta\},\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}}}.
\]
For arbitrary classes, character-block preservation holds for $\Gamma$-invariant Novikov specializations, as explained in Corollary~\ref{cor:quantum-blocks}.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:GS-isomorphism_intro}
For $k=0,1$ there is a noncanonical $\mathbb C[\![z]\!]$-linear isomorphism
\[
 \widehat\Phi^{H,\mathrm{add}}_{T,k}:
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(X)\xrightarrow{\,\sim\,}
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(\widehat X,\alpha_T)
\]
reducing to the chosen nonequivariant comparison. Via the completed Chern characters this is an isomorphism of completed complexified $K$-groups. It is not asserted to be multiplicative, canonical, kernel-induced, or a map of equivariant spectra.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:F_Z_intro}
Under the independently specified kernel, coefficient-theory, and convolution hypotheses \textup{(C1)--(C4)} of Theorem~\ref{thm:cohomological-95}, the completed cohomological kernel transform intertwines the reduced two-point operators. Its
rigidified Chen--Ruan realization is
$$\Phi_P^{\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}=\mathsf J^{-1}\mathsf S_{\mathrm{age}}^{-1}\Phi^H_{\Xi_P},\quad \text{and }\Phi^H_{\Xi_P}=\widehat{\Phi}^{H,\mathrm{add}}_{T},$$
and
\begin{equation}\label{diagram_FM_Steinberg_intro}
 F^{\widehat X,\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}_{\bar\beta}\Phi_P^{\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}
   =\Phi_P^{\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}F^X_\beta.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
This is a sufficient criterion, not an unconditional compatibility theorem. In particular, character decomposition does not imply its convolution hypothesis.  Compatibility with full quantum divisor operators additionally requires the classical divisor terms and Novikov degrees to be matched.  

Theorem \ref{thm:F_Z_intro} implies that the Fourier-Mukai transform $\text{FM}_{\mathcal{P}}$ is compatible with the quantum product. Hence this implies the Monodromy conjecture saying that the quantum connection and the Fourier-Mukai transformation have the same Monodromy  once the Fourier-Mukai kernel can be extended to the full Hitchin base $\mathbb A$, see \cite{BMO}, \cite{MO}.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:theta-descent}
There is a unique class $\widehat\Theta_T\in H_T^2(\widehat X,\mathbb Q)$ with $q^*\widehat\Theta_T=\Theta_T$. The same statement holds for rational equivariant Chow classes of codimension one.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Tensoring preserves the equivariant first Chern class of the chosen determinant line by Lemma~\ref{lem:theta-symplectic-invariant}. For a finite group, rational transfer gives
$q^*:H_T^*(\widehat X,\mathbb Q)\simeq H_T^*(X,\mathbb Q)^\Gamma$. The Chow version follows from
$q_*q^*=|\Gamma|$ and $q^*q_*a=\sum_\eta\tau_\eta^*a$. Thus $\widehat\Theta_T=|\Gamma|^{-1}q_*\Theta_T$ has the claimed pullback, and injectivity proves uniqueness.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:smooth}
The variety \(X\) is smooth and
\[
 \dim_\mathbb C X=2(r^2-1)(g-1).
\]
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
If an endomorphism \(a:E\to E\) commutes with \(\phi\), stability implies that \(a\) is scalar. Since the deformation complex uses
\(\operatorname{End}_0(E)\),
\(
 \mathbb H^0(C,\mathcal C^\bullet_{(E,\phi)})=0
\). 
The trace pairing
\[
 \operatorname{End}_0(E)\otimes\operatorname{End}_0(E)\longrightarrow\mathcal O_C
\]
together with Serre duality identifies the degree-two hypercohomology with the dual of degree zero one:
\[
 \mathbb H^2(C,\mathcal C^\bullet_{(E,\phi)})
 \cong
 \mathbb H^0(C,\mathcal C^\bullet_{(E,\phi)})^\vee
 =0.
\]
Thus \((E,\phi)\in\mathfrak X_\Lambda\) is unobstructed and its infinitesimal deformation space is
\(
 \mathbb H^1(C,\mathcal C^\bullet_{(E,\phi)})
\).

Riemann--Roch gives
\[
 \chi(\operatorname{End}_0(E))=(r^2-1)(1-g), \quad \text{and }
 \chi(\operatorname{End}_0(E)\otimes K_C)=(r^2-1)(g-1).
\]
Hence
\[
 \chi(\mathcal C^\bullet)
 =
 \chi(\operatorname{End}_0(E))-\chi(\operatorname{End}_0(E)\otimes K_C)
 =
 -2(r^2-1)(g-1).
\]
Since the degree-zero and degree-two hypercohomology vanish,
\[
 \dim \mathbb H^1
 =
 -\chi(\mathcal C^\bullet)
 =
 2(r^2-1)(g-1).
\]
The determinant-framed stack \(\mathfrak X_\Lambda\) has only the finite central stabilizer \(\mu_r\), with no infinitesimal stabilizer. This stabilizer acts on \eqref{eq:def-complex} by conjugation and hence acts trivially on \(\mathbb H^1\). Therefore the smooth gerbe \(\mathfrak X_\Lambda\to X\) has trivial stabilizer action on its local deformation space, and its coarse space \(X\) is smooth with
$T_{(E,\phi)}X =\mathbb H^1(C,\mathcal C^\bullet_{(E,\phi)})$ and the displayed dimension.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:omega-weight}
For the Higgs-scaling action,
\[
 t^*\omega=t\,\omega.
\]
Thus \(\omega\) has \(T\)-weight \(1\).
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
At the level of the deformation complex, a tangent vector consists schematically of a deformation of the bundle and a deformation of the Higgs field. The symplectic form pairs the bundle deformation in one tangent vector with the Higgs-field deformation in the other, minus the reverse pairing. Higgs scaling acts with weight \(0\) on the bundle direction and weight \(1\) on the Higgs-field direction. Every summand in the symplectic pairing therefore has weight \(1\).
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:hitchin-proper}
The Hitchin morphism \(h:X\to\mathbb A\) is proper, hence projective.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Properness of the characteristic-polynomial morphism for the moduli of semistable pairs can be found in \cite[Theorem 6.1]{Nitsure}; see also \cite{HitchinSI}. The fixed-determinant and trace-free locus is obtained by restricting to a closed condition and to the corresponding linear subspace of the Hitchin base, so properness is preserved by base change and passage to the closed subspace.

The variety \(X\) is quasi-projective by the GIT construction. A proper quasi-projective morphism is projective; see e.g. \cite[Th\'eor\`eme~5.5.3(ii)]{EGAII}. Thus \(h\) is projective.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:vir-red}
For every \(\beta\ne0\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:vir-red}
 [{\mathcal M}_{n,\beta}]^{\mathrm{vir}}_T
 =c_1^T(\mathbb C_1)\cap[{\mathcal M}_{n,\beta}]^{\mathrm{red}}_T
 =\hbar[{\mathcal M}_{n,\beta}]^{\mathrm{red}}_T .
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
This is \eqref{eq:abstract-excess} with \(\mathcal L=\mathcal O\otimes\mathbb C_1\). Since \(c_1^T(\mathbb C_1)=\hbar\), the sign is positive: the removed obstruction quotient is the weight-\(+1\) line.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
After forgetting equivariance the quotient line is trivial, so \([{\mathcal M}_{n,\beta}]^{\mathrm{vir}}=0\).  This also follows directly from Kiem--Li cosection localization, since the degeneracy locus is empty. The equivariant Euler class of the removed line gives the nonzero factor \(\hbar\).
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:basicness}
Let \(S\) be a smooth integral scheme, let \(\pi:{\mathcal C}\to S\) be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected genus-zero curves, and let \(F:{\mathcal C}\to X\) be a morphism. There is a unique \(\eta_F\in H^0(S,\Omega_S^2)\) such that
\[
 F^*\omega=\pi^*\eta_F.
\]
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Since \(\pi\) is smooth of relative dimension one, the cotangent filtration gives
\[
 0\longrightarrow\pi^*\Omega_S^2
 \longrightarrow\Omega_{\mathcal C}^2
 \longrightarrow
 \pi^*\Omega_S^1\otimes\Omega_{{\mathcal C}/S}^1
 \longrightarrow 0.
\]
For a smooth proper genus-zero family,
\[
 \pi_*\Omega_{{\mathcal C}/S}^1=0,
 \qquad
 \pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}=\mathcal O_S.
\]
The projection formula therefore shows that the last term has no global sections, whereas
\[
 H^0({\mathcal C},\pi^*\Omega_S^2)=H^0(S,\Omega_S^2).
\]
Thus every regular two-form on \({\mathcal C}\), in particular \(F^*\omega\), is the pullback of a unique two-form on \(S\).
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:nodal-basicness}
Let \(\pi:\mathcal D\to S\) be a proper flat family of connected nodal curves of arithmetic genus $0$ over a smooth integral scheme. Let \(s_1,s_2:S\to\mathcal D\) be sections through the smooth locus, and let \(F:\mathcal D\to X\).  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:marking-forms}
 (F\circ s_1)^*\omega=(F\circ s_2)^*\omega \quad\text{in }H^0(S,\Omega_S^2).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
First, shrink to a dense equisingular open subset of \(S\). After a finite \'etale surjective base change, the components, nodes, and branches are labelled, and the simultaneous normalization is a disjoint union of smooth proper genus-$0$ families
\[
 \bigsqcup_a {\mathcal C}_a\longrightarrow S.
\]
Write \(F_a:{\mathcal C}_a\to X\) for the induced maps. By Lemma \ref{lem:basicness},
\[
 F_a^*\omega=\pi_a^*\eta_a
\]
for two-forms \(\eta_a\) on \(S\). If branch sections \(q_a:S\to {\mathcal C}_a\) and \(q_b:S\to {\mathcal C}_b\) form a node, then
\(F_a\circ q_a=F_b\circ q_b\), whence
\[
 \eta_a=q_a^*F_a^*\omega
 =(F_a\circ q_a)^*\omega
 =(F_b\circ q_b)^*\omega
 =q_b^*F_b^*\omega=\eta_b.
\]
The dual graph (which is a tree) is connected, so all \(\eta_a\) are equal. Pulling back at the two marked sections proves \eqref{eq:marking-forms} after the \'etale cover, and faithfully flat descent proves it before the cover.

Finally, the two sides of \eqref{eq:marking-forms} are regular sections of the locally free sheaf \(\Omega_S^2\). Equality on the dense equisingular open subset extends over all of \(S\). This extension is what includes tangent
directions which smooth nodes occurring only in special fibers; moving markings and moving node sections were already included in the argument.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:isotropy}
Let \(W\subset {\mathcal M}_{2,\beta}\) be an integral locally closed substack, and let
\[
 Z=\overline{(\operatorname{ev}_1,\operatorname{ev}_2)(W)}\subset X\times X.
\]
Then
\[
 \Omega|_{Z_{\mathrm{sm}}}=0.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \dim Z\le m.
\]
If \(\dim Z=m\), then \(Z\) is Lagrangian.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Choose an irreducible component of an \'etale scheme atlas of \(W\) which dominates \(W\), and replace it by a dense smooth integral open \(S\). Pull back the universal curve, its two sections, and its map to \(X\). Applying Lemma \ref{lem:nodal-basicness} gives
\[
 g^*\Omega=0, \qquad g=(\operatorname{ev}_1,\operatorname{ev}_2)|_S:S\longrightarrow X\times X.
\]
Finite stabilizers cause no issue, since the identity of differential forms is \'etale local on the source.

The morphism \(S\to Z\) is dominant. Over \(\mathbb C\), the induced extension of function fields is separable, so generic smoothness gives a dense open of \(Z_{\mathrm{sm}}\) over which \(dg:T_sS\to T_lZ\) is surjective at general points.  The equality \(g^*\Omega=0\) then implies \(\Omega|_{T_lZ}=0\). As \(\Omega|_{Z_{\mathrm{sm}}}\) is a regular two-form, vanishing on a dense open implies vanishing everywhere on \(Z_{\mathrm{sm}}\). Thus \(Z\) is isotropic. Since \(X\times X\) is symplectic of dimension \(2m\), every isotropic subvariety has dimension at most \(m\), and equality is exactly the Lagrangian condition.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
The argument does not use the virtual fundamental class. This is important: it controls the geometric support of the entire stable-map stack and thereby excludes equivariant terms supported on subvarieties of dimension \(>m\).
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:Y-isotropic}
Every irreducible component of \(Y_\beta\) is isotropic in \((X\times X,\Omega)\). Hence
\[
 \dim Y_\beta\le m.
\]
Every \(m\)-dimensional irreducible component of \(Y_\beta\) is a \(T\)-invariant Steinberg subvariety.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Apply Proposition \ref{prop:isotropy} to irreducible components of \({\mathcal M}_{2,\beta}\) whose images dominate the irreducible components of \(Y_\beta\), and use \eqref{eq:fiber-product-support}. If an image has dimension \(m\), it is
Lagrangian. Since \(T\) is connected, it preserves every member of the finite set of irreducible components of the \(T\)-stable scheme \(Y_\beta\). Thus each top-dimensional component is a Steinberg subvariety.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:top-equiv-chow}
Let \(Y\) be a finite-type \(T\)-scheme of dimension at most \(m\). Then \(A_m^T(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\) is the \({\mathbb Q}\)-span of the equivariant fundamental classes of the \(m\)-dimensional irreducible components of \(Y\). In particular, no positive power of \(\hbar\) can occur as the coefficient of a higher-dimensional geometric support, because such a support does not exist.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
We use the finite-dimensional approximation \cite{EG}: consider
\[
 U_N=\mathbb A^N\setminus\{0\},
\]
on which \(T\) acts freely by scalar multiplication. The $N$-th Borel construction is 
\begin{equation}\label{eqn:Nth_Borel}
Y\times^T U_N.
\end{equation}
 For \(N\) sufficiently large in the range under consideration, we have 
\[
 A_m^T(Y)
 =
 A_{m+N-1}(Y\times^T U_N).
\]
The mixed quotient has dimension at most \(m+N-1\). Hence its Chow group in dimension \(m+N-1\) is generated by the fundamental classes of its top-dimensional irreducible components. Those components occur precisely from the \(m\)-dimensional \(T\)-invariant irreducible components of \(Y\). Because \(T\) is connected, it preserves each member of the finite set of irreducible components. This proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:Z-Steinberg}
For every \(\beta\ne0\), the class
\[
 Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}} = (\operatorname{ev}_1,\operatorname{ev}_2)_*[{\mathcal M}_{2,\beta}]^{\mathrm{red}}_T
\]
is a finite linear combination of (classes of) Steinberg subvarieties with $\mathbb{Q}$-coefficients. Hence the standard evaluation cycle satisfies
\[
 C_\beta=\hbar  Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}} =\hbar\sum_j c_{\beta,j}[L_{\beta,j}]_T
 \quad\text{in }A_{m-1}^T(Y_\beta)_{\mathbb Q}.
\]
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The reduced virtual class has complex dimension \(m\) by \eqref{eq:vdim-reduced}. Since the evaluation map is proper, we have 
\[
  Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}} \in A_m^T(Y_\beta)_{\mathbb Q}.
\]
By Corollary \ref{cor:Y-isotropic},
\[
 \dim Y_\beta\le m.
\]
Apply Lemma \ref{lem:top-equiv-chow}. We obtain
\[
  Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}} = \sum_j c_{\beta,j}[L_{\beta,j}]_T, \qquad c_{\beta,j}\in{\mathbb Q}\setminus \{0\},
\]
where the \(L_{\beta,j}\) are the \(m\)-dimensional irreducible components that occur with nonzero coefficient. By
Corollary \ref{cor:Y-isotropic}, each \(L_{\beta,j}\) is Lagrangian and lies in \(X\times_\mathbb A X\). Hence each is a Steinberg subvariety.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
We give another proof of the existence of the Steinberg factor after evaluation, which does not use equation \eqref{eq:red-class-kernel}. Forgetting the torus action, the everywhere surjective Kiem--Li cosection has empty degeneracy locus. Their cosection localization theorem therefore gives
\[
 [{\mathcal M}_{2,\beta}]^{\mathrm{vir}}=0.
\]
It follows that the image of \(C_\beta\in A_{m-1}^T(Y_\beta)_{\mathbb Q}\) under the forgetful map to \(A_{m-1}(Y_\beta)_{\mathbb Q}\) is zero. Brion's augmentation theorem for arbitrary finite-type torus schemes \cite[Corollary~2.3.1]{Brion} states that
\[
 A_*^T(Y_\beta)/(\hbar)\cong A_*(Y_\beta),
 \qquad T={\mathbb C}^*.
\]
Hence there exists \(\delta_\beta\in A_m^T(Y_\beta)_{\mathbb Q}\) with
\[
 C_\beta=\hbar\delta_\beta.
\]
By Corollary \ref{cor:Y-isotropic} and Lemma \ref{lem:top-equiv-chow}, \(\delta_\beta\) is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of the \(m\)-dimensional Lagrangian components of \(Y_\beta\). This proves the required Steinberg divisibility independently. The Brion lift can be nonunique when \(\hbar\)-torsion is present; the kernel-cone construction gives the distinguished lift \(\delta_\beta= Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}}\).
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
(Comparison with \cite{MO})
For an equivariant symplectic resolution $X\to X_0$, Maulik--Okounkov state that the pushforward of the reduced two-point virtual class is a rational linear combination of Steinberg correspondences \cite[\S 7.2.1]{MO}. The preceding argument proves the analogous assertion for the smooth coprime Higgs moduli space directly, using the Hitchin morphism in place of the affinization map.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:divisor}
For every divisor \(D\) equipped with an equivariant lift \(D_T\),
\[
 M_D
 =
 D_T\cup
 +
 \hbar\sum_{\beta>0}(D\cdot\beta)q^\beta\mathbf{F}_{Z_{2,\beta}^{\mathrm{red}}}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 \frac{M_D-D_T\cup}{\hbar}
 \in
 \operatorname{Act}\!\left(\widehat{\mathsf S}_{\rm cyc}(X/\mathbb A)\right).
\]
Taking \(D=\Theta\) gives the formula for $\Theta$ in Theorem  \ref{thm:main}.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:lift-independence}
If \(D_T'\) and \(D_T\) are two equivariant lifts of the same ordinary divisor, then the positive-degree parts of their quantum multiplication operators agree.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
The equivariant divisor equation in \eqref{eq:divisor-equation} uses only the degree of the underlying ordinary divisor on \(\beta\). Both lifts have the same underlying class, so their coefficients \(D\cdot\beta\) are equal for every 
\(\beta\). The positive-degree formula in Theorem \ref{thm:divisor} is therefore unchanged. The classical operators differ by cup product with \(D_T'-D_T\), and no assertion that this difference is a scalar is needed.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem_hitchin_constant_twisted}
Every connected proper twisted curve maps constantly to the affine Hitchin base. Every two-point evaluation image of a genus-zero twisted stable-map family is isotropic in the product of its sector symplectic forms, with the difference sign.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
A morphism from a twisted curve to an affine scheme factors through the coarse curve, whose global regular functions are constant. This also holds in families, and defines the Hitchin-value map. Properness of twisted stable maps
to a proper tame target, applied relatively over $\mathbb A$, makes the evaluation maps proper; bounded degree is measured by an ample line on the coarse target \cite{AGV}.

For isotropy, shrink a smooth parameter space to a dense equisingular open and label components and branches after an \'etale cover. The normalizations are smooth proper twisted genus-zero families. For a smooth twisted rational curve with coarse map $c$, a local root coordinate $z=x^s$ shows $(c_*\Omega^1)=(\Omega^1_{\mathbb P^1})$: an invariant regular differential is a regular multiple of $x^{s-1}dx=dz/s$. Hence the pushforward of relative one-forms has no sections and the pushforward of the structure sheaf is $\mathcal O$. The cotangent-filtration proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:basicness} therefore applies on each component. The pulled-back two-form is basic. At a node its two restrictions agree after pullback to the branch gerbe, so the basic forms agree on adjacent components and hence on the whole tree. Pullback at the marking gerbes gives equality of the two evaluation forms. The gerbes can be neutralized \'etale locally for this calculation, and the equality descends. Extension over the parameter space and generic smoothness prove isotropy, exactly as in Proposition~\ref{prop:isotropy}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{defn_Steinberg_PGL}
For an input on $\overline{\mathcal F}_1$, the contribution with second marking in $\overline{\mathcal F}_2$ to the output on $\bar\iota(\overline{\mathcal F}_2)$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Act-def_stacky}
 F^{\widehat X,\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}_{\bar\beta}(a)
  :=\sum_{\mathcal F_2}s_{\mathcal F_2}
   \operatorname{PD}^{-1}_{\bar\iota(\overline{\mathcal F}_2)}
    (\check\operatorname{ev}_2)_*\left(\operatorname{ev}_1^*a\cap[\mathfrak M_{2,\bar\beta} (\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2)]^{\mathrm{red}}_T\right).
\end{equation}
Cycle classes are understood in the Borel--Moore expression. The factor $s_{\mathcal F_2}$ is forced by the pairing (\ref{eqn:pairing_2}). The operator preserves Chen--Ruan degree; on underlying ordinary cohomology the degree shift is $2(a_{\mathcal F_1}-a_{\mathcal F_2})$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:divisor_PGL_r}
For an untwisted divisor $D\in H^2(\widehat X,\mathbb Q)$ with equivariant lift $D_T$,
\[
 M_D=D_T\cup_{\operatorname{CR}}(-)+
   \hbar\sum_{\bar\beta>0}(D\cdot\bar\beta) q^{\bar\beta}F^{\widehat X,\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}_{\bar\beta}.
\]
Its positive-degree correction is sectorwise Steinberg-valued with the normalizations in Definition~\ref{defn_Steinberg_PGL}.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Pair the proposed operator with a class on the second marking sector. The output factor $s_{\mathcal F_2}$ cancels the pairing factor $1/s_{\mathcal F_2}$, and the inversion converts the tested output back to $\operatorname{ev}_2^*b$. The result is exactly the reduced two-point invariant. Multiplication by $\hbar$ recovers the standard invariant. The orbifold divisor equation for an untwisted insertion \cite{AGV} gives $(D\cdot\bar\beta)$; the degree-zero term is $D_T\cup_{\operatorname{CR}}-$. Nondegeneracy after localization proves the formula.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:discriminant}
For every \(\beta\ne0\), we have
\[
 \operatorname{Supp} Z_\beta^{\mathrm{red}}
 \subset
 h^{-1}(\Delta)\times_\mathbb A h^{-1}(\Delta).
\]
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{lem:hitchin-constant}, every genus-$0$ stable map lies in one Hitchin fiber. If its Hitchin value lies in
\(\mathbb A^{\mathrm{sp,sm}}\), the restriction of the map to every irreducible \(\mathbb P^1\)-component is constant. Thus
the entire connected stable map is constant, contradicting \(\beta\ne0\).
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:theta-symplectic-invariant}
The action of $\Gamma$ commutes with $T$, preserves $\Omega_X$, and fixes $\Theta_T$ in rational equivariant Chow and cohomology.
\begin{equation}\label{eq:theta-invariant}
 \tau_\eta^*\Theta_T=\Theta_T.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
The identification $\operatorname{End}_0(E\otimes\eta)=\operatorname{End}_0(E)$ preserves the trace pairing on the deformation complex \eqref{eq:def-complex}. It therefore preserves the symplectic form and commutes with Higgs scaling. Use the normalization of \eqref{eq:theta-Euler-zero}, then the auxiliary bundle $F_0$ has rank $r$ and degree $r(g-1)-d$, where $d=\deg\Lambda$. Therefore
\[
 \chi(C,E\otimes F_0)=r\deg F_0+rd+r^2(1-g)=0.
\]
The determinant line
\begin{equation}\label{eq:theta-detline}
 \mathscr L_{F_0}=\det R\pi_*(\mathcal E\otimes F_0)^{-1}
\end{equation}
has trivial scalar weight and descends from the fixed-determinant stable Higgs moduli stack. Its linearization is the one induced by the action on the universal Higgs object; Higgs scaling leaves the underlying bundle unchanged.
Tensoring by $\eta$ replaces $F_0$ by $F_0\otimes\eta$. On the universal $\mu_r$-gerbe, equivariant Grothendieck--Riemann--Roch and $\operatorname{ch}(\eta)=1$ in rational Chow imply 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:theta-GRR}
 c_1^T(\mathscr L_{F_0\otimes\eta})=c_1^T(\mathscr L_{F_0}).
\end{equation}
Pullback to that gerbe is an isomorphism on rational equivariant Chow; thus this global equality descends to $X$. In particular, there is no undetermined multiple of $\hbar$ in \eqref{eq:theta-invariant}.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:red-invariance}
Postcomposition by $\tau_\eta$ identifies the reduced cycle for $\beta$ with that for $(\tau_\eta)_*\beta$. Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diagonal-invariance}
 (\tau_\eta\times\tau_\eta)_*Z_\beta^{\mathrm{red}} =Z_{(\tau_\eta)_*\beta}^{\mathrm{red}}.
\end{equation}
For a finite $\Gamma$-stable set $B$ of nonzero effective curve classes, put 
$Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}=\sum_{\beta\in B}Z_\beta^{\mathrm{red}}$ and let $\mathbf F_B$ be its correspondence operator. Then $Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}$ is
symmetric and diagonally $\Gamma$-invariant.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The differential of $\tau_\eta$ identifies the standard obstruction complexes and commutes with the symplectic cosections. It identifies the intrinsic cones inside the kernels and hence their zero-section Gysin classes. This uses the kernel-cone construction, not an unproved reduced perfect obstruction theory. Proper evaluation pushforward gives \eqref{eq:diagonal-invariance}. Summation over $B$ gives diagonal invariance; interchange of markings gives symmetry.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:block-decomposition}
For every such $B$ and every character $\kappa$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbf F_{B,\kappa}
 &=\mathbf F_B\mathsf P_\kappa
  =\mathsf P_\kappa\mathbf F_B
  =\mathsf P_\kappa\mathbf F_B\mathsf P_\kappa,
       \label{eq:block-operator}\\
 Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}&=\sum_\kappa Z_{B,\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}},
       \label{eq:block-kernel-sum}\\
 (Z_{B,\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}})^{\mathsf t}&=Z_{B,\kappa^{-1}}^{\mathrm{red}}.
       \label{eq:inverse-character-transpose}
\end{align}
In particular, individual blocks are symmetric for $r=2$; in general, symmetry is guaranteed for self-inverse characters, not for every character. For $\kappa\ne1$ the two theta contractions vanish in equivariant Chow:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nontrivial-contractions}
 (p_2)_*(p_1^*\Theta_T\cap Z_{B,\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}})=0,
 \qquad
 (p_1)_*(p_2^*\Theta_T\cap Z_{B,\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}})=0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Diagonal invariance and symmetry give, for $g=\tau_\eta$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kernel-move-action}
 (g\times\operatorname{id})_*Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}=(\operatorname{id}\times g^{-1})_*Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}.
\end{equation}
The projection formula therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:operator-equivariance}
 \mathbf F_Bg^*=g^*\mathbf F_B,
\end{equation}
where all cohomological pushforwards use Poincar\'e duality as in \eqref{eq:Act-def}. Also
\begin{equation}\label{eq:first-factor-action}
 \mathbf F_{(g\times\operatorname{id})_*Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}}=\mathbf F_Bg^*.
\end{equation}
Averaging gives \eqref{eq:block-operator}; character orthogonality gives \eqref{eq:block-kernel-sum}. For transposition, substitute
$\xi=\eta^{-1}$:
\[
 (Z_{B,\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}})^{\mathsf t}
 =\frac1{|\Gamma|}\sum_\eta\kappa(\eta)^{-1}
          (\tau_\eta^{-1}\times\operatorname{id})_*Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}
 =\frac1{|\Gamma|}\sum_\xi\kappa(\xi)
          (\tau_\xi\times\operatorname{id})_*Z_B^{\mathrm{red}}
 =Z_{B,\kappa^{-1}}^{\mathrm{red}}.
\]
Finally, theta-invariance and the projection formula imply
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Chow-character-contraction}
 (p_2)_*(p_1^*\Theta_T\cap Z_{B,\kappa}^{\mathrm{red}})
 =\left(\frac1{|\Gamma|}\sum_\eta\kappa(\eta)^{-1}\right)(p_2)_*(p_1^*\Theta_T\cap Z_B^{\mathrm{red}})=0.
\end{equation}
Transposition and $\kappa^{-1}\ne1$ give the second contraction.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:quantum-blocks}
The full theta operator is equivariant for the semilinear action 
$\tau_\eta^*\otimes(q^\beta\mapsto q^{(\tau_\eta^{-1})_*\beta})$. After any Novikov specialization invariant under the curve-class action, it preserves the character decomposition \eqref{eq:cohomology-character-decomposition}. For an individually invariant class $\beta>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:quantum-character-blocks}
 [q^\beta](\Theta\star-)|_{H_T^*(X)_\kappa}
   =(\Theta\cdot\beta)\hbar\,\mathbf F_{\{\beta\},\kappa}.
\end{equation}
For an orbit sum, the analogous formula is the sum of these weighted operators over the orbit. After invariant specialization, the theta-square correction is in the trivial character block.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Functoriality gives $\tau_\eta^*\mathbf F_\beta(\tau_\eta^*)^{-1}=\mathbf F_{(\tau_\eta^{-1})_*\beta}$. Theta degrees are unchanged, so this identity proves semilinear equivariance of the Novikov series. An invariant specialization makes
the action on its coefficients trivial. Apply the theorem to each orbit; nontrivial character blocks annihilates $\Theta_T$.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{rem:not-source-splitting}
This is a Fourier decomposition of evaluation correspondences, not a geometrically disjoint decomposition of the stable-map space or of its virtual class. It does not determine the individual irreducible $L_{\beta,j}$ in \eqref{eq:Zbeta-Steinberg}, their multiplicities, or their Chow-theoretic support. The endoscopic interpretation below uses an
additional direct-image support theorem.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:fixed-endoscopic-base}
Let \(X^\gamma\) be the fixed locus of tensorization by \(\gamma\). Its Hitchin image is contained in
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Agamma}
 \mathbb A_\gamma =\{s^2\, | \, s\in H^0(C,K_C\otimes\gamma)\}\subset \mathbb A.
\end{equation}
The closure of the image equals \(\mathbb A_\gamma\). In particular, \(\mathbb A_\gamma\) is a one-dimensional linear subspace of 
\(\mathbb A\).
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
A fixed stable Higgs bundle admits an isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-isomorphism}
 \psi:(E,\phi)\xrightarrow{\sim}(E\otimes\gamma,
 \phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_\gamma).
\end{equation}
Stability implies that an automorphism of \((E,\phi)\) is scalar. After rescaling \(\psi\), the square of \(\psi\) is the identity. The pair \((E,\psi)\) is therefore a module over
\(\mathcal O_C\oplus\gamma^{-1}=(\pi_{\gamma})_*\mathcal O_{C_\gamma}\). It has the form
\begin{equation}\label{eq:E-pushforward}
 E\cong(\pi_{\gamma})_* L
\end{equation}
for a line bundle \(L\) on \(C_\gamma\); this is the usual fixed-point description of Narasimhan--Ramanan \cite{NarasimhanRamanan}.

The Higgs-isomorphism condition in \eqref{eq:fixed-isomorphism} makes the Higgs field linear over the \'etale algebra in \eqref{eq:etale-cover}. After pullback to \(C_\gamma\), it is therefore diagonal. The trace-free condition says that the two eigenvalues sum to $0$, so the eigenvalue is anti-invariant. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diagonal-higgs}
 \pi_\gamma^*\phi =\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\0&-s\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 s\in H^0(C,K_C\otimes\gamma).
\end{equation}
Its characteristic polynomial is \(\lambda^2-s^2\). Hence \(h(E,\phi)=s^2\), proving the containment.

Conversely, let \(0\neq s\in H^0(C,K_C\otimes\gamma)\). The norm map \(\operatorname{Nm}:\operatorname{Pic}(C_\gamma)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)\) is surjective on the required degree component: on \(\operatorname{Pic}^0\), its composite with pullback is multiplication by $2$, and multiplication by $2$ on an abelian variety is surjective. The determinant of a finite pushforward satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:determinant-norm-formula}
 \det((\pi_{\gamma})_*L)=\operatorname{Nm}(L)\otimes\det((\pi_{\gamma})_*\mathcal O_{C_\gamma}).
\end{equation}
We may therefore choose \(L\) with \(\det((\pi_{\gamma})_*L)=\Lambda\).

Let \(\Sigma_s\subset\operatorname{Tot}(K_C)\) be the spectral curve \(\lambda^2=s^2\). Its normalization is the connected \'etale cover \(C_\gamma\), and  the two local roots are exchanged by the nontrivial cocycle defining 
\(\gamma\). The zeros of $s$ are two distinct Weierstrass points, by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-torsion-labels} and \eqref{eq:Kgammaij} below. At each zero, the normalization identifies the two points above it, and $\Sigma_s$ has an ordinary node. In particular, \(\Sigma_s\) is integral, although it need not be smooth. The spectral sheaf associated with \(((\pi_{\gamma})_*L,\phi)\) is the rank-one torsion-free sheaf obtained from \(L\) by finite pushforward to 
\(\Sigma_s\).

The generic fiber of \(\Sigma_s\to C\) is \(\operatorname{Spec}K(C_\gamma)\), which is a field because the \'etale double cover is connected. A \(\phi\)-invariant line subbundle would give a one-dimensional invariant subspace over 
\(K(C)\), hence a \(K(C)\)-rational eigenvalue and a splitting of this quadratic field extension. This is impossible.  Equivalently, the BNR correspondence identifies such a subbundle with a spectral subsheaf whose generic support is a degree-one component of \(\Sigma_s\); see \cite[Section~3]{BNR}. The integral spectral curve has no such component. Hence the resulting Higgs bundle is stable. Thus every nonzero point of \(\mathbb A_\gamma\) occurs in the Hitchin image of 
\(X^\gamma\), and taking the closure gives equality. Equation \eqref{eq:h0-Kgamma} shows that \(\mathbb A_\gamma\) is a line.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:two-torsion-labels}
The line bundles
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gammaij}
 \gamma_{ij}=\mathcal O_C(w_i-w_j),
 \qquad 1\leq i<j\leq6,
\end{equation}
are the fifteen nonzero elements of \(\mathop{\rm Jac}\nolimits(C)[2]=({\mathbb Z}/2{\mathbb Z})^4\).
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
The divisor \(2w_i\) is a fiber of the hyperelliptic pencil.  Hence
\(2w_i\sim2w_j\), and \(\gamma_{ij}^2\cong\mathcal O_C\).
The line bundle \(\gamma_{ij}\) is nontrivial, since distinct points of a
positive-genus curve are not linearly equivalent.

Suppose \(\gamma_{ij}=\gamma_{k\ell}\).  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:degree-two-equivalence}
 w_i+w_\ell\sim w_k+w_j.
\end{equation}
If the divisor on the left moves, it belongs to the unique hyperelliptic pencil. A fiber containing a Weierstrass point is twice that point, so \(i=\ell\). The divisor on the right then also belongs to the pencil, which forces \(k=j\). The two unordered pairs are the same. Otherwise the divisor on the left is rigid. Linear equivalence in \eqref{eq:degree-two-equivalence} then implies equality of the two effective divisors, and again the unordered pairs agree. Thus the $15$ classes in \eqref{eq:gammaij} are distinct. Since \(|\mathop{\rm Jac}\nolimits(C)[2]|=2^{2g}=16\), they exhaust the nonzero elements.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:explicit-endoscopic-lines}
For \(1\leq i<j\leq6\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Agamma-Hij}
 \mathbb A_{\gamma_{ij}}=H_i\cap H_j.
\end{equation}
For comparison, the ordinary squaring map on \(H^0(C,K_C)\) has image the quadratic cone
\begin{equation}\label{eq:square-cone}
 Q=\{\ell^2\, |\, \ell\in H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(1))\}\subset \mathbb A.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Use \(K_C\cong\mathcal O_C(2w_j)\). Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Kgammaij}
 K_C\otimes\gamma_{ij} \cong\mathcal O_C(w_i+w_j).
\end{equation}
A nonzero section of this line bundle, unique up to scalar, has divisor \(w_i+w_j\). Its square has divisor 
\(2w_i+2w_j\), which is the pullback of \(b_i+b_j\). Under \eqref{eq:A-binary-quadratics}, the square therefore spans the line of binary quadratics vanishing at both \(b_i\) and \(b_j\). This line is \(H_i\cap H_j\).

The space \(H^0(C,K_C)\) is two-dimensional. Its squares form the affine cone over the Veronese conic in
\(\mathbb P H^0(C,K_C^2)\). This is \(Q\). This comparison does not identify \(Q\) with the support of the trivial character: the identity fixes all of \(X\), and the stable direct-image summand is supported on all of \(\mathbb A\).
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:discriminant-decomposition}
The reduced Hitchin discriminant is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:discriminant-decomposition}
 \Delta_{\mathrm{red}}=Q\cup H_1\cup\cdots\cup H_6.
\end{equation}
A general point of \(H_i\) gives an integral spectral curve with one node. A general point of \(Q\) gives two copies of \(C\) meeting transversely in two points.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
A Hitchin coordinate is a binary quadratic \(a\in H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(2))\). Its pullback to \(C\) has a multiple
zero in exactly two cases. First, the two roots of \(a\) coincide; then \(a=\ell^2\) and \(a\in Q\). Second, one root is a branch point \(b_i\); then \(a\in H_i\). These conditions give \eqref{eq:discriminant-decomposition} set-theoretically, and each component is reduced at its generic point.

For the local types, write the hyperelliptic map near a ramification point as \(w=z^2\). At a general point of \(H_i\), the spectral equation is \(\lambda^2-z^2u=0\), with \(u\) a unit, and has one ordinary node. At a general point of 
\(Q\), write \(a=\ell^2\). Then \((\lambda-\ell)(\lambda+\ell)=0\), and the two components meet transversely at the two simple zeros of \(\ell\).
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
\label{rem:discriminant-versus-endoscopy}
The six divisors \(H_i\) are generic nodal discriminant components. They are not the nontrivial endoscopic bases. The latter are the $15$ codimension-two intersections \(H_i\cap H_j, 1\leq i< j\leq 6\).
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{thm:endoscopic-support-external}
Let \(h:X\to \mathbb A\) be the trace-free, fixed-determinant rank-$2$ Hitchin fibration with \(\gcd(2,\deg\Lambda)=1\). For every \(0\neq\gamma\in\mathop{\rm Jac}\nolimits(C)[2]\) and every integer \(j\), we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:endoscopic-support-perverse}
 \operatorname{Supp}\bigl({}^p\!\mathcal H^j ({\mathcal K}_{\kappa_{\gamma,\deg\Lambda}})\bigr)\subset \mathbb A_\gamma.
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:endoscopic-support}
 {\mathcal K}_{\kappa_{\gamma,\deg\Lambda}}|_{\mathbb A\setminus \mathbb A_\gamma}=0.
\end{equation}
The summand \({\mathcal K}_1\) is the stable, or invariant, summand. The nontrivial summands are the variant, or endoscopic, summands.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
This is the coprime fixed-determinant specialization of \cite[Theorem~0.2]{MS}. The support construction is given in
\cite[Section~3]{MS}. The degree-dependent character in that theorem is \eqref{eq:degree-dependent-character}. Its hypotheses apply because the rank is $2$ and the determinant degree is odd. The endoscopic base in their notation is the image of \(H^0(C,K_C\otimes\gamma)\) under the square map. It is therefore \(\mathbb A_\gamma\) in \eqref{eq:Agamma}.
The rank-$2$ stable--variant identification is also described in \cite[Sections~4.4--4.5]{DCHM}. Its original mirror-symmetry formulation is \cite{HT}. We use only the support inclusion \eqref{eq:endoscopic-support-perverse}. We do not use equality of supports or a compactly supported variant.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:stable-endoscopic-blocks}
The endomorphism \(\mathbf{F}_{Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{B}}\) preserves \eqref{eq:direct-image-decomposition}. Its block on \({\mathcal K}_1\) is the stable block. For \(0\neq\gamma\in\Gamma\), its block
\begin{equation}\label{eq:endoscopic-block}
 \mathbf{F}_{Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{B},\gamma}
 :=\mathbf{F}_{Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{B},\kappa_\gamma}:{\mathcal K}_{\kappa_\gamma}\longrightarrow{\mathcal K}_{\kappa_\gamma}
\end{equation}
is induced by the cycle class of \(Z_{B,\kappa_\gamma}^{\mathrm{red}}\) and is supported on \(\mathbb A_\gamma\), in the sense that its restriction to \(\mathbb A\setminus \mathbb A_\gamma\) is $0$. In genus $2$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:endoscopic-block-line}
 \operatorname{Supp}(\mathbf{F}_{Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{B},\gamma_{ij}}) \subset H_i\cap H_j.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Proposition~\ref{prop:red-invariance} makes \(\mathbf{F}_{Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{B}}\) a \(\Gamma\)-equivariant endomorphism. It therefore commutes with every character projector and preserves each direct summand. For \(\gamma\neq0\), the source and target of the block \eqref{eq:endoscopic-block} restrict to $0$ on \(\mathbb A\setminus \mathbb A_\gamma\) by Theorem
\ref{thm:endoscopic-support-external}. The block has the same property. Equation \eqref{eq:endoscopic-block-line} follows from Theorem \ref{thm:explicit-endoscopic-lines}.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:generic-no-variant}
Let \(D^\circ\) be a dense open subset of one of \(Q,H_1,\ldots,H_6\), obtained by deleting all pairwise intersections and all worse spectral strata. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:variant-zero-generic-D}
 {\mathcal K}_{\kappa_\gamma}|_{D^\circ}=0
\end{equation}
for every \(\gamma\neq0\). Hence every endoscopic block of \(\mathbf{F}_{Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{B}}\) restricts to $0$ on 
\(D^\circ\).
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Every nontrivial endoscopic base is a line \(H_i\cap H_j\), and this line is deleted from each \(D^\circ\). Apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:endoscopic-support-external}.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
\label{rem:Chow-support-warning}
Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-endoscopic-blocks} does not assert that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unsupported-Chow-claim}
Z_{B,\kappa_\gamma}^{\mathrm{red}}
\in
\operatorname{Im}\left[A_6^T(X_{\mathbb A_\gamma}\times_{\mathbb A_\gamma}X_{\mathbb A_\gamma})\longrightarrow A_6^T(X\times_\mathbb A X)\right].
\end{equation}
The projected kernel may contain homologically trivial pieces away from \(\mathbb A_\gamma\). Establishing \eqref{eq:unsupported-Chow-claim} would require a separate Chow-theoretic support theorem.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:equivariant-gerbe}
Fix a banded $\mu_r$-gerbe,
\[
 \mathcal G_T\longrightarrow \widehat X=[X/\Gamma],
\]
which represents the lifting class $\alpha$, together with a coherent lift of the Higgs-scaling $T$-action to $\mathcal{G}_T$. The $T$-action is required to commute with the quotient-groupoid structure. Write
\[
 \alpha_T\in\operatorname{Br}_T(\widehat X)[r]
\]
for the class of this fixed equivariant twist, $\alpha$ for its underlying nonequivariant twist, and $\widetilde\alpha_T$ for its topological realization. No canonicity among equivariant structures is asserted.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
\label{rem:gerbe-construction}
Choose $c_0\in C$ and evaluate the universal projective bundle on the $\text{PGL}_r$ moduli stack at $c_0$. Its lifting gerbe for $1\to\mu_r\to\operatorname{SL}_r\to\operatorname{PGL}_r\to1$ is a banded $\mu_r$-gerbe. A coherent Higgs-scaling action on this evaluated projective object induces an equivariant lifting datum as in Definition~\ref{def:equivariant-gerbe}. We fix the datum and the identification of its underlying twist with the one used in the nonequivariant comparison as inputs. Lifts of a projective bundle \emph{on the whole curve} differ by $r$-torsion line bundles and form, when nonempty, a $\Gamma$-torsor of isomorphism classes. That fibered category must not be substituted for the single $\mu_r$-gerbe just described.
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
For an integer $k$, a finite-type $T$-space or finite quotient stack $Z$, and a $T$-equivariant local system $\mathscr L$, set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:periodic-degree}
 H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(Z;\mathscr L):=\bigoplus_{n\in{\mathbb Z}}H_T^{k-2n}(Z;\mathscr L)u^n.
\end{equation}
Multiplication by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:zdef}
 z:=\hbar u^{-1}
\end{equation}
preserves total degree. Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:zcompletion}
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(Z;\mathscr L):=\varprojlim_N H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(Z;\mathscr L)/(z^N).
\end{equation}
For the quotient stack $\widehat{X}$, set
\begin{align}
 H^k_{T,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(\widehat X,\alpha_T)
 &:={\bigoplus_{\mathcal F\in\pi_0(I\widehat X)}}
 H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(\mathcal F;\mathscr L_{\alpha_T,\mathcal F}),
 \label{eq:delperiodic}\\
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(\widehat X,\alpha_T)
 &:={H^k_{T,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(\widehat X,\alpha_T)}^{\wedge}_{(z)}.
 \label{eq:completed-delperiodic}
\end{align}
There is no Chen--Ruan age shift in these definitions. Multiplication by $u$ identifies degree $k$ with degree $k+2$, so $k=0,1$ suffice.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:point-test}
One has
\[
 H^0_{T,\operatorname{per}}(\mathrm{pt})=\mathbb C[z],\qquad
 \widehat H^0_{T,\operatorname{per}}(\mathrm{pt})=\mathbb C[\![z]\!].
\]
If one instead keeps only parity and completes $\mathbb C[\hbar]\otimes\mathbb C[u,u^{-1}]$ at $(\hbar)$, the result is not finite
free over $\mathbb C[\![\hbar]\!]$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
In total degree zero, the only monomials are $\hbar^ju^{-j}=z^j$. If total degree is forgotten, every Laurent
monomial $u^n$ survives independently, giving infinitely many module generators over $\mathbb C[\![\hbar]\!]$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:semiprojective}
The $T$-varieties $X$ and $X^\gamma$, for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$, are smooth semiprojective varieties, and their $T$-fixed loci are projective and every point has a limit as $t\to0$.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
All weights on $\mathbb{A}$ are positive, so $\mathbb{A}^T=\{0\}$. Hence $X^T\subset h^{-1}(0)$, which is projective because $h$ is proper. The fixed locus of a finite-order automorphism of a smooth complex variety is smooth. Thus $X^\gamma$ is smooth, and $(X^\gamma)^T=X^\gamma\cap X^T$ is projective.

For $x\in X$, the Hitchin image of the orbit extends to $t=0$ by
\[
 t\longmapsto(t^2a_2,\ldots,t^ra_r).
\]
The valuative criterion for the proper map $h$ uniquely extends the corresponding $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C(\!(t)\!)$-point of $X$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[\![t]\!]$. Its special point is $\lim_{t\to0}t\cdot x$.  If $x\in X^\gamma$, uniqueness and commutation of the two actions show that the limit remains in $X^\gamma$.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:stabilizer-trivial}
Let a connected complex algebraic group $G$ act trivially on a connected space $F$. If $\mathscr L$ is a $G$-equivariant local system on $F$, the stabilizer action on every fiber is trivial. Hence
\[
 H_G^\bullet(F;\mathscr L) \cong H^\bullet(F;\mathscr L)\otimes H^\bullet(BG;\mathbb C).
\]
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Restrict the equivariance isomorphism to $G\times\{x\}$. It is an automorphism of a constant local system and is therefore locally constant in $G$. Connectedness makes it constant, and the cocycle condition at the identity forces it to be the identity. The Borel construction then has the exterior-product coefficient system, and the K\"unneth theorem applies.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{thm:equivariant-formality}
Let $Z$ be a smooth semiprojective finite-type complex $T$-variety and let $\mathscr L$ be a finite-rank, finite-monodromy, $T$-equivariant local system. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $H_T^\bullet(Z;\mathscr L)$ is finite free over $\mathbb C[\hbar]$;

\item the forgetful map induces
\[
 H_T^\bullet(Z;\mathscr L)/(\hbar) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^\bullet(Z;\mathscr L);
\]

\item for every $k$, $H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(Z;\mathscr L)$ is finite free over $\mathbb C[z]$, reduction modulo $z$ is ordinary fixed-degree periodized cohomology, and its completion is finite free over $\mathbb C[\![z]\!]$.
\end{enumerate}
The same conclusions hold after taking invariants under a finite group action commuting with $T$ and preserving $\mathscr L$.
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
A finite-monodromy algebraic local system is a direct summand of the pushforward of the constant system from a finite \'etale cover. For an equivariant local system the cover can be chosen $T$-equivariant: use the finite monodromy cover of the Borel local system and pull it back to $Z$. The connected stabilizers act trivially on its finite fibers. The cover is smooth and semiprojective. Indeed it is finite over $Z$, its fixed locus is projective, and the lifted algebraic orbit extends across zero by properness. It suffices to prove the constant coefficient assertion on this cover and then take the appropriate finite-group representation summand.

The filtrable Bia\l ynicki--Birula decomposition has strata which are affine bundles of rank $a_i$ over smooth projective fixed components $F_i$. Their compactly supported cohomology is $H_c^j(\text{stratum}_i)=H^{j-2a_i}(F_i)(-a_i)$ and is pure of weight $j$. Induction on the closed filtration, using its compact-support long exact sequence, proves purity of $H_c^j(Z)$: the boundary maps between degrees $j$ and $j+1$ vanish because their weights differ. Poincar\'e duality then gives purity of $H^j(Z)$ of weight $j$.

The Borel spectral sequence
\[
 E_2^{p,q}=H^p(BT)\otimes H^q(Z)\Longrightarrow H_T^{p+q}(Z)
\]
is a spectral sequence of mixed Hodge structures, as seen on algebraic finite Borel approximations. Each $E_2^{p,q}$ is pure of weight $p+q$; every differential changes that weight by one. It therefore degenerates. The edge map to $H^*(Z)$ is surjective. Homogeneous lifts of a finite basis, together with the spectral-sequence filtration, give a free
$\mathbb C[\hbar]$-basis and the asserted reduction modulo $\hbar$. The same argument on the finite cover followed by the finite-monodromy summand proves (i)--(ii) for $\mathscr L$.

If $a_j$ are homogeneous lifts, then in fixed degree $k$ the elements $a_j u^{(k-\deg a_j)/2}$ with $\deg a_j\equiv k\pmod2$ form a $\mathbb C[z]$-basis. This proves (iii). For an additional finite group, Reynolds averaging is an exact projector preserving all filtrations; its image is a finite projective, hence free, module over $\mathbb C[\hbar]$ and over $\mathbb C[z]$. Invariants commute with reduction and completion.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:fixed-degree-description}
For a connected inertia component $\mathcal F=[F/\Gamma_F]$, put
\[
 V^k_{\mathcal F}:=
 \bigoplus_{p\equiv k\, (2)} H^p(\mathcal F;\mathscr L_{\alpha,\mathcal F})u^{(k-p)/2}.
\]
Then $\widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(\mathcal F;\mathscr L_{\alpha_T,\mathcal F})$ is finite free over $\mathbb C[\![z]\!]$, its reduction is $V^k_{\mathcal F}$, and, after choosing homogeneous equivariant lifts, there is an isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-degree-expansion}
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(\mathcal F;\mathscr L_{\alpha_T,\mathcal F})
 \cong V^k_{\mathcal F}\widehat\otimes_\mathbb C\mathbb C[\![z]\!].
\end{equation}
The reduction and associated graded are canonical; the displayed splitting need not be canonical.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:equivariant-formality} to $F$ and then take $\Gamma_F$-invariants. The basis construction in its proof gives \eqref{eq:fixed-degree-expansion}.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:finite-KCW}
The analytic spaces $X$ and $X^\gamma$, with their actions of $K$ and of any commuting subgroup of $\Gamma$, have finite equivariant CW  homotopy type. Finite equivariant covers have the same property.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
In the differential-geometric description of Higgs moduli, the squared norm of the Higgs field is a proper moment map for the circle action \cite{HitchinSD,HauselCompactification}. The tensor action of the finite group $\Gamma$ is isometric and preserves this function. Restriction to a fixed locus $X^\gamma$ is again a proper Hamiltonian circle moment map; the fixed locus is a smooth K\"ahler submanifold. Its critical set is its circle-fixed locus. There are finitely many compact critical components, and the Hamiltonian circle local normal form makes the function Morse--Bott, with finite-rank equivariant negative normal bundles.
Equivariant Morse theory therefore gives finitely many disk-bundle attachments over compact critical manifolds. Those manifolds, carrying only the residual finite-group action, have finite equivariant triangulations \cite{IllmanTriangulation}. The attachments give finite $K$-equivariant CW homotopy type, simultaneously with the commuting finite group. A finite equivariant cover carries the pullback K\"ahler form and proper moment map. Its critical manifolds are finite covers of the preceding compact ones, so the same argument applies.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:trace-block-finite-generation}
For $k=0,1$, $M^k=\operatorname{KU}_{K\times G}^k(V;\tau_T)\otimes\mathbb C$ is finite over $R_K$. The same holds for finite relative equivariant CW pairs.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Use induction on equivariant cells. A cell has stabilizer a closed subgroup $H\subset K\times G$. If $H$ is finite, its (twisted) representation group has finite complex dimension. Otherwise $H^0=K$, and $H/K$ is finite. The corresponding finite central
extension for the twist has only finitely many weight classes modulo tensoring with $\chi$; within each class a finite group has finitely many irreducible representations. Thus its twisted representation module is finite over $R_K$. The six-term exact sequences for cell attachment and noetherianess of $R_K$ complete the induction. The same argument applies to relative pairs.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:relative-completion}
For $k=0,1$ there is a natural isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:relative-completion}
 (\operatorname{KU}_T^k(Y,\tau_T)\otimes\mathbb C)^{\wedge}_{I_T}
   \xrightarrow{\sim}
 \varprojlim_N\bigl(\operatorname{KU}^k(Y_N,\tau_N)\otimes\mathbb C\bigr).
\end{equation}
The statement also holds for finite relative equivariant CW pairs. The finite-stage complexified tower is Mittag--Leffler, and its $\varprojlim^1$ vanishes. No completion in the finite-$G$ direction occurs.
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Apply the equivariant Thom exact sequence to the representation disk $D(\mathbb C^{N+1})$ and sphere $E_N$, crossed with $V$ and with the same pulled-back twist. The Euler class is $t^{N+1}$, so it yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sphere-completion-sequence}
 0\longrightarrow M^k/t^{N+1}M^k
 \longrightarrow \operatorname{KU}^k(Y_N,\tau_N)\otimes\mathbb C
 \longrightarrow M^{k+1}[t^{N+1}]\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Here the bracket denotes the subgroup killed by $t^{N+1}$, and $k+1$ is read modulo two. Naturality of the Thom class for $\mathbb C^{N+1}\subset\mathbb C^{N+2}$ identifies transition maps on the right with multiplication by $t$. On a finite $R_K$-module the $t$-primary
torsion is killed by a fixed power of $t$. The right-hand tower is therefore pro-zero.  The middle tower is pro-isomorphic to the left adic quotient tower, whose maps are surjective. Taking the inverse limit proves the claim and the Mittag--Leffler assertion. The disk, sphere and Thom arguments apply equally to a relative pair.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- remark-11: body_md -->
\label{rem:compensated-isotropy}
Let $V=K$ with $K$ acting by translation and $G=\mu_2$ acting by multiplication by $-1$. The nontrivial element $g\in G$ has no fixed point on $V$. Nevertheless $K\times G$ has stabilizer generated by $(-1,g)$, whose nontrivial trace block in equivariant $K$-theory is nonzero. In that block $\chi=-1$, so $\chi-1$ is invertible and
circle-relative completion annihilates the block. Thus literal $g$-fixed loci cannot in general describe uncompleted equivariant trace blocks. We do not posit an integral invertible $\operatorname{KU}$-module local system whose monodromy is an arbitrary complex character: a root of unity need not be an integral unit in $\pi_0\operatorname{KU}=\mathbb Z$.
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{thm:general-completed-ch}
Under these hypotheses, the finite-stage complex twisted delocalized Chern characters induce a natural isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-completed-ch}
 \widetilde\operatorname{ch}^{\wedge}_{T,\tau,u}:
 (\operatorname{KU}_T^k(Y,\tau_T)\otimes\mathbb C)^{\wedge}_{I_T}
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(Y,\tau_T),
 \qquad k=0,1.
\end{equation}
The target uses ordinary fixed-locus degrees on unrigidified inertia, not Chen--Ruan age shifts. The coefficient-ring map is $\chi\mapsto e^z$.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
At each finite free Borel approximation, only the finite group $G$ remains. The complex twisted delocalized Chern character \cite{FHT} gives
\[
 \operatorname{KU}^k(Y_N,\tau_N)\otimes\mathbb C \xrightarrow{\sim}H^k_{\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(Y_N,\tau_N),
\]
naturally in $N$. Here $(E_N\times_KV)^g=E_N\times_KV^g$, since $K$ acts freely on $E_N$. Theorem~\ref{thm:relative-completion} identifies the inverse limit on the left.
On each fixed sector, the equivariant sphere Gysin sequence has Euler class $\hbar^{N+1}$. In fixed total degree, after multiplication by the compensating power  of Bott variable, its Euler class is $z^{N+1}$. The cohomological version of \eqref{eq:sphere-completion-sequence} therefore has a quotient term by $z^{N+1}$ and a torsion term in the opposite parity, with transition multiplication by $z$. Finite equivariant CW type makes these periodized modules finite over $\mathbb C[z]$, by the same cell induction as in Lemma \ref{lem:trace-block-finite-generation}. The torsion tower is pro-zero. The limit on the right is consequently the $z$-adic completion. Finite-group invariants and the finite inertia sum commute with this construction. The point computation \eqref{eq:weight-line-character} identifies the coefficient map.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:completed-ch}
For $k=0,1$, Theorem~\ref{thm:general-completed-ch} gives natural isomorphisms
\begin{align}
 \operatorname{ch}_{T,u}^{\wedge}:
 \left(\operatorname{KU}_T^k(X)\otimes\mathbb C\right)^{\wedge}_{I_T}
 &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(X),
 \label{eq:completed-source-ch}\\
 \widetilde\operatorname{ch}_{T,\alpha,u}^{\wedge}:
 \left(\operatorname{KU}_T^k(\widehat X,\widetilde\alpha_T)\otimes\mathbb C\right)^{\wedge}_{I_T}
 &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(\widehat X,\alpha_T).
 \label{eq:completed-target-ch}
\end{align}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:equivariant-formality}, both targets are finite free
$\mathbb C[\![z]\!]$-modules; reduction modulo $z$ is the ordinary and twisted
delocalized nonequivariant periodic Chern character.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
For $X$, take $G=1$. For $\widehat X=[X/\Gamma]$, take $G=\Gamma$. 
Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-KCW} verifies the finite $K$-CW hypothesis, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:equivariant-formality} together with
Corollary~\ref{cor:fixed-degree-description} give the finite freeness and the reduction statements.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{thm:supported-completion}
Assume that $(W,W\setminus Z)$ is represented by a finite $(K\times G)$-CW pair and that the twist and coefficient systems are finite. Put $W_N=E_N\times_KW$ and $Z_N=E_N\times_KZ$. Then, for $k\in{\mathbb Z}/2$, there are natural isomorphisms
\begin{equation}\label{eq:supported-completion}
 \left(\operatorname{KU}^k_{T,Z}(W,\tau_T)\otimes\mathbb C\right)^{\wedge}_{I_T}
 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \varprojlim_N\bigl(\operatorname{KU}^k_{Z_N}(W_N,\tau_N)\otimes\mathbb C\bigr)
 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \widehat H^k_{T,Z,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(W,\tau_T).
\end{equation}
The two inverse systems are Mittag--Leffler; no $\varprojlim^1$ term occurs. The identifications are natural for morphisms of relative pairs, pullback, products, and excision.
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Use the relative-pair form of Theorem~\ref{thm:relative-completion} for $(W,W\setminus Z)$. Its proof is the sphere Thom sequence \eqref{eq:sphere-completion-sequence}, with the relative twisted groups in place of $M^k$; the same finite-generation and pro-zero torsion arguments apply. At finite Borel approximations, the complex delocalized
Chern character is an isomorphism on relative pairs by the absolute isomorphism and the long exact sequence. On each inertia component, the relative sphere Gysin sequence similarly identifies the inverse limit with $z$-adic completion of cohomology with support. These constructions are natural for maps of pairs, products and excision, and both towers are pro-isomorphic to their surjective adic quotient towers. Proper pushforward is treated separately by Riemann--Roch; no unsupported integral trace-coefficient construction is involved.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\label{thm:additive-lift}
For $k=0,1$, there exists a noncanonical $\mathbb C[\![z]\!]$-linear isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:additive-lift}
 \widehat\Phi^{H,\mathrm{add}}_{T,k}:
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{per}}(X)
 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(\widehat X,\alpha_T)
\end{equation}
whose reduction modulo $z$ is $\Phi^H_{\operatorname{GS},k}$. Via Theorem~\ref{thm:completed-ch}, this is equivalent to a noncanonical isomorphism of the completed complexified equivariant $K$-groups as $\widehat R_T$-modules.
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:completed-ch} and Corollary~\ref{cor:fixed-degree-description}, the source and target of \eqref{eq:additive-lift} are finite free $\mathbb C[\![z]\!]$-modules.  Their reductions modulo $z$ are the source and target of $\Phi^H_{\operatorname{GS},k}$, so they have the same rank. Choose bases lifting bases of the reductions and let $B\in\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb C)$ be the matrix of $\Phi^H_{\operatorname{GS},k}$. The same constant matrix over $\mathbb C[\![z]\!]$ is invertible and gives \eqref{eq:additive-lift}.

If $\Phi_1$ and $\Phi_2$ are two lifts, then $U=\Phi_2\Phi_1^{-1}$ is an automorphism congruent to the identity modulo $z$; conversely every such $U$ produces another lift.  This proves noncanonicity and shows why the construction carries none of the
additional structures excluded in the statement.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:genuine-equivariant}
Suppose, as an independent input, that there is a $T$-equivariant equivalence of twisted $\operatorname{KU}$-spectra
\[
 \Phi^{\operatorname{KU},T}:\operatorname{KU}_T(X)\xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }
 \operatorname{KU}_T(\widehat X,\widetilde\alpha_T)
\]
whose forgetful map is \eqref{eq:GS-noneq}. Then completion and Theorem~\ref{thm:completed-ch} canonically produce completed additive maps \eqref{eq:additive-lift}. If the spectrum equivalence is induced by a global supported $T$-equivariant twisted kernel, its completed cohomological realization is the full inertial Riemann--Roch transform of that kernel, not an arbitrary matrix lift.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Complete the assumed spectrum equivalence at $I_T$ and conjugate its maps on homotopy groups by the natural isomorphisms in Theorem~\ref{thm:completed-ch}. A kernel-induced assertion additionally uses Theorem~\ref{thm:bivariant-RR} below.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:symplectic-age}
For every connected inertia component $\mathcal F$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:component-dimension}
 d_{\mathcal F}=m-2a_{\mathcal F},\qquad
 a_{\mathcal F}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
\end{equation}
Inversion sends $\mathcal F$ to a component $\iota(\mathcal F)$ with
$d_{\iota(\mathcal F)}=d_{\mathcal F}$ and $a_{\iota(\mathcal F)}=a_{\mathcal F}$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
The $\Gamma$-action preserves the holomorphic symplectic form. On the moving tangent space, an eigenvalue $e^{2\pi i\theta}$ with $0<\theta<1$ is paired with
$e^{-2\pi i\theta}=e^{2\pi i(1-\theta)}$. Each paired two-dimensional summand contributes $1$ to the age and $2$ to the complex codimension of $F$. Summing proves \eqref{eq:component-dimension} and integrality. Replacing $\gamma$ by $\gamma^{-1}$ exchanges the paired eigenvalues and leaves both the fixed locus and the total contribution unchanged.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:two-point-monodromy}
Let a connected genus-zero twisted nodal curve carry a principal $\Gamma$-bundle and two marked monodromies $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:monodromy-product}
 \gamma_1\gamma_2=1.
\end{equation}
Consequently the two-evaluation cycle has labels $(\gamma,\gamma^{-1})$. After the output involution in Definition~\ref{defn_Steinberg_PGL}, the operator has label
$\gamma\to\gamma$. If both marked monodromies are trivial, all node monodromies are trivial and the bundle is trivial on each geometric source curve. Over a family it can be a nontrivial pullback of a $\Gamma$-torsor on the base.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
On the normalization of each irreducible component, the product of the monodromies at marked points and node branches is $1$. Multiply these relations over all vertices of the tree dual graph. The two balanced monodromies at each node are inverse and cancel, giving \eqref{eq:monodromy-product}.

If the marked monodromies are both $1$, take a leaf of the dual tree. The relation on that component forces its unique node monodromy to be $1$. Remove the leaf and iterate. The bundle is then trivial on every coarse $\mathbb P^1$ because
$H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(\mathbb P^1,\Gamma)=0$, and the gluing class is trivial because the dual graph is a tree.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:canonical-rigidification-descent}
Let $\alpha_T$ be a banded, ungraded finite gerbe. On every connected unrigidified sector $\mathcal F$ represented by $(\gamma,F)$, the cyclic subgroup $\langle\gamma\rangle$ acts trivially on the transgression line
$\mathscr L_{\alpha_T,\mathcal F}$. Consequently, there is a canonical descended line
$\overline{\mathscr L}_{\alpha_T,\overline{\mathcal F}}$ and a canonical isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:line-descent}
 \rho_{\mathcal F}^*\overline{\mathscr L}_{\alpha_T,\overline{\mathcal F}}
 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \mathscr L_{\alpha_T,\mathcal F}.
\end{equation}
They are compatible with inversion and the unit; fusion and associativity are compared after pullback to the common unrigidified multiple-inertia correspondences.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Fix a geometric point $x\in F$ and an object of the gerbe over $x$. Its isotropy is a central extension
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sector-central-extension}
 1\longrightarrow\mu_r\longrightarrow
 \widetilde{\Gamma_x}\longrightarrow\Gamma_x\longrightarrow1.
\end{equation}
The fiber of the transgression line at $(x,\gamma)$ is the weight-one line associated to the $\mu_r$-torsor of lifts of $\gamma$. If $\widetilde\gamma$ is one lift, the centralizer acts on this torsor by conjugation. For every $\zeta\in\mu_r$,
\[
 \widetilde\gamma(\zeta\widetilde\gamma)
 \widetilde\gamma^{-1}=\zeta\widetilde\gamma,
\]
so $\gamma$ acts trivially on the associated line. The same calculation with $\widetilde\gamma^j$ shows that every element of $\langle\gamma\rangle$ acts trivially.  Because the extension is central, this conclusion is independent of the chosen object and lift. It is functorial under restriction in $x$, hence glues over the entire sector.
Lemma~\ref{lem:rigidification-descent} now gives the canonical descent.

Inversion sends a lift to its inverse, fusion multiplies two lifts, and the unit uses the identity lift. These operations commute with the central extension, and multiplication in $\widetilde{\Gamma_x}$ is associative. Thus the descended lines carry inversion and unit identifications; the fusion and associativity identifications agree after pullback to the common unrigidified multiple-inertia spaces.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:rigidification-descent}
Let $\rho:\mathcal F\to\overline{\mathcal F}$ be a gerbe banded by a finite cyclic group $H$, and let $\mathscr L$ be a rank-one local system on $\mathcal F$. Then $\mathscr L$ is isomorphic to the pullback of a local system on $\overline{\mathcal F}$ if and only if the inertia action of $H$ on one, equivalently every, fiber of $\mathscr L$ is trivial. Under this condition, rational pullback is an isomorphism and
\[
 \rho_*\rho^*=\frac1{|H|}\operatorname{id},
 \qquad (\rho^*)^{-1}=|H|\rho_*.
\]
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
The assertion is local on $\overline{\mathcal F}$ for a topology in which the gerbe is neutral. On such a chart the morphism is $BH\times U\to U$. A local system on $BH\times U$ is a local system on $U$ together with a representation of $H$ on its fiber, and it is a pullback precisely when that representation is trivial. These local descents glue because pullback is fully faithful on the trivial-isotropy summand. The pushforward formulas follow.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
\label{thm:quotient-formula}
There is a canonical equivalence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:trivial-map-stack}
 \mathfrak N_B^{\operatorname{triv}}\simeq[\mathfrak M_B/\Gamma],
\end{equation}
where $\Gamma$ acts by postcomposition. In equivariant Borel--Moore homology, or in rational equivariant Chow groups, one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:quotient-pullback}
 (q\times q)^*Z_B^{\widehat X,\operatorname{triv}}
 =\sum_{\eta\in\Gamma}(\operatorname{id}\times\tau_\eta)_*Z_B^X
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:quotient-pushforward}
Z_B^{\widehat X,\operatorname{triv}}=\frac1{|\Gamma|}(q\times q)_*Z_B^X.
\end{equation}
If $\beta$ itself is $\Gamma$-invariant, this specializes to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:single-beta-quotient}
 Z_{\{\beta\}}^{\widehat X,\operatorname{triv}}=\frac1{|\Gamma|}(q\times q)_*Z_\beta^X.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
After an \'etale localization on the parameter scheme, an object of 
$\mathfrak N_B^{\operatorname{triv}}$ admits a trivialization of its principal bundle and is then exactly a stable map to $X$ of class in $B$. To see that the bundle is locally pulled back from the base, its restriction to one identity marking defines a base torsor. The scheme of trivializations on each genus-zero fiber is the same torsor, because that fiber has trivial finite \'etale fundamental group. Proper base change for the finite bundle, or the relative scheme of these trivializations, gives the asserted identification in families. Changing the trivialization by $\eta\in\Gamma$ postcomposes the lift by $\tau_\eta$. Descent therefore gives \eqref{eq:trivial-map-stack}.  Automorphism groups are retained by the quotient-stack description, so no informal passage to coarse spaces occurs.

Now base-change the two evaluation maps by the atlas $q\times q:X^2\to\widehat X^2$. A lift of the first marked evaluation fixes a trivialization of the principal $\Gamma$-bundle at the first marking. Relative to it, a lift at the second marking differs by a
unique element $\eta\in\Gamma$. Consequently there is a canonical disjoint-union presentation
\begin{equation}\label{eq:evaluation-base-change}
 \mathfrak N_B^{\operatorname{triv}}\times_{\widehat X^2}X^2
 \simeq\coprod_{\eta\in\Gamma}\mathfrak M_B,
\end{equation}
and the evaluation on the $\eta$-summand is $(\operatorname{ev}_1,\tau_\eta\circ\operatorname{ev}_2)$. Flat pullback of the reduced cycle along the finite \'etale atlas and proper base change for evaluation give \eqref{eq:quotient-pullback}.

The map $q\times q$ has degree $|\Gamma|^2$, hence
\[
 (q\times q)_*(q\times q)^*=|\Gamma|^2
\]
on rational Chow and Borel--Moore homology. Moreover $q\circ\tau_\eta=q$, so pushing \eqref{eq:quotient-pullback} forward gives
\[
 |\Gamma|^2Z_B^{\widehat X,\operatorname{triv}}=|\Gamma|(q\times q)_*Z_B^X.
\]
Division by $|\Gamma|^2$ proves \eqref{eq:quotient-pushforward}, and the single-class formula follows. Since the identity sector has $s_{\mathcal F}=1$, rigidification does not change this calculation.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
For the degree-zero diagonal, \eqref{eq:quotient-pushforward} gives
\[
 \frac1{|\Gamma|}(q\times q)_*[\Delta_X] =[\Delta_{\widehat X}],
\]
because $\Delta_X\to\Delta_{\widehat X}$ has degree
$|\Gamma|$.  This is a useful check that the factor is neither $1$ nor
$1/|\Gamma|^2$.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:formal-transport}
Fix one additive lift $\widehat\Phi^{H,\mathrm{add}}_{T,k}$ from
Theorem~\ref{thm:additive-lift} and an endomorphism $F_X$ of its source. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:formal-transport}
 F_{\widehat X}^{\mathrm{transport}}
 :=\widehat\Phi^{H,\mathrm{add}}_{T,k}
 F_X(\widehat\Phi^{H,\mathrm{add}}_{T,k})^{-1}
\end{equation}
is the unique endomorphism intertwined with $F_X$ by that chosen lift. If a second lift is $U\widehat\Phi^{H,\mathrm{add}}_{T,k}$, then
\[
 F_{\widehat X}^{\mathrm{transport}\prime}
 =UF_{\widehat X}^{\mathrm{transport}}U^{-1}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
The intertwining identity follows by direct substitution, and uniqueness follows by multiplying on the right by the inverse of the chosen lift. The change-of-lift formula is equally immediate. Since the matrix lift in Theorem~\ref{thm:additive-lift} is arbitrary beyond its residue modulo $z$, all geometric properties of the transported operator require separate proof.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:common-support}
For closed $T$-invariant subsets $Z\subset Z'\subset W$, the inclusions of relative pairs give canonical extension-of-support maps
\[
 \operatorname{KU}^*_{T,Z}(W;\tau)\longrightarrow\operatorname{KU}^*_{T,Z'}(W;\tau),
 \qquad
 \widehat H^*_{T,Z,\operatorname{per}}(IW;\mathscr M)
 \longrightarrow
 \widehat H^*_{T,Z',\operatorname{per}}(IW;\mathscr M).
\]
If two supported kernels have respective closed supports $Z_L$ and $Z_R$ in the same ambient outer product, an equality between them means the equality of their canonical images in the group with support $Z_L\cup Z_R$. This convention is used in both $K$-theory and completed cohomology and is compatible with pullback, product, fusion, and proper supported pushforward.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:K-convolution}
Under the preceding properness and perfectness hypotheses,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:K-composition}
 \Phi^{\operatorname{KU}}_{L_{12}\star_{\operatorname{KU}}L_{01}}
 =\Phi^{\operatorname{KU}}_{L_{12}}\circ\Phi^{\operatorname{KU}}_{L_{01}}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, a type-correct ambient-product kernel identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:K-intertwining-kernels}
P\star_{\operatorname{KU}}K_X=K_{\widehat X}\star_{\operatorname{KU}}P
\end{equation}
implies the corresponding intertwining identity of $K$-theory operators. If the two proper outer supports are $Z_L$ and $Z_R$, then \eqref{eq:K-intertwining-kernels} is, by
Definition~\ref{def:common-support}, an equality in
\[
 \operatorname{KU}^0_{T,Z_L\cup Z_R}
 \bigl(W_{02},\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_0^*\alpha_0^{-1}\otimes\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_2^*\alpha_2\bigr).
\]  
If $P$ has a convolution inverse $Q$, the transported kernel is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:K-transported-kernel}
 K_{\widehat X}=P\star_{\operatorname{KU}}K_X\star_{\operatorname{KU}}Q.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
Pull the input and the two kernels to $W_{012}$. Associativity of the $\operatorname{KU}$-product, the projection formula, and functoriality of supported complex-oriented pushforward identify the transform of \eqref{eq:K-convolution} with the iterated transform. The stated properness is exactly what permits both supported pushforwards. The intertwining and transport assertions follow by applying this composition formula and, for the last assertion, convolving with $Q$.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
\label{rem:identity-test}
If $Y_i=Y_j=\mathbb A$, both structure maps are the identity, and the kernel is the supported class $\Delta_!1\in\operatorname{KU}^0_{T,\Delta_\mathbb A}(\mathbb A\times\mathbb A)$, then \eqref{eq:K-transform} is the identity. The relative projection is the ordinary ambient projection
