$\mathbb A\times \mathbb A\to \mathbb A$, restricted to diagonal support. This test rules out the earlier convention that treated the fiber product itself as the ambient kernel space while retaining the ambient-product degree and Todd normalization.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:H-convolution}
Assume the pulled-back supports in \eqref{eq:H-convolution} are proper over the outer product. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:H-composition}
 \Phi^H_{\Xi_{12}\star_H\Xi_{01}}
 =\Phi^H_{\Xi_{12}}\circ\Phi^H_{\Xi_{01}}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, an equality
\begin{equation}\label{eq:H-intertwining-kernels}
 \Xi_P\star_H\Xi_X=\Xi_{\widehat X}\star_H\Xi_P
\end{equation}
of ambient-product, coefficient-valued supported kernels implies the corresponding intertwining identity on completed unshifted delocalized cohomology. Sectorwise, if the two proper outer supports are $Z_L$ and $Z_R$, the equality is taken in the explicit common group
\[
 \widehat H^0_{T,Z_L\cup Z_R,\operatorname{per}}
 \bigl(\mathcal F_0\times\mathcal F_2;
 \mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_0^*\mathscr L_0^\vee\otimes\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_2^*\mathscr L_2\bigr).
\]
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Substitute \eqref{eq:H-transform} twice. The two periodic factors are $u^{d_0+d_1}$, which is the product of the outer factor $u^{d_0}$ and the middle factor in 
\eqref{eq:H-convolution}. The projection formula moves the first supported pushforward past the pullback of the second kernel, and functoriality identifies the iterated integration with the pushforward along $\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{02}$. Fusion cancels the middle transgression lines. This proves \eqref{eq:H-composition}; applying it to the two
sides of \eqref{eq:H-intertwining-kernels} proves the last assertion.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{defn_Td_quotient_stack}
Let $Y=[V/G]$ be a smooth finite quotient stack with a commuting $T$-action. On a connected component $\mathcal F\subset IY$ represented by $F\subset V^g$, decompose the moving normal bundle as $N_{F/V}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ne1}N_\lambda$. If $x_{\lambda,j}$ are the $T$-equivariant Chern roots, put
\begin{align}
 D^T_{\mathcal F}(Y)
 &:=\prod_{\lambda\ne1}\prod_j
   \bigl(1-\lambda^{-1}e^{-x_{\lambda,j}}\bigr),
 \label{eq:moving-denominator}\\
 \widetilde\operatorname{Td}_T(TY)|_{\mathcal F}
 &:=\frac{\operatorname{Td}_T(T\mathcal F)}{D^T_{\mathcal F}(Y)}.
 \label{eq:orbifold-Todd}
\end{align}
The denominator has invertible degree-zero term. For an even class $c=\sum c_{2j}$, write $c_u=\sum c_{2j}u^{-j}$.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\label{thm:bivariant-RR}
Assume the state spaces and all relative pairs in question satisfy the finite equivariant CW hypotheses of Theorems~\ref{thm:general-completed-ch} and
\ref{thm:supported-completion}. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \eqref{eq:tau-orb-definition} is a well-defined completed supported class with exactly the coefficient line in \eqref{eq:trace-character-type}.

\item For $k\in{\mathbb Z}/2$, the diagram
\begin{equation}\label{eq:RR-square}
\begin{CD}
 (\operatorname{KU}_T^k(Y_i,\alpha_i)\otimes\mathbb C)^{\wedge}_{I_T}
 @>{\Phi^{\operatorname{KU}}_{L_{ij}}}>>
 (\operatorname{KU}_T^k(Y_j,\alpha_j)\otimes\mathbb C)^{\wedge}_{I_T}\\
 @V{\widetilde\operatorname{ch}^{\wedge}_{T,\alpha_i,u}}V{\cong}V
 @VV{\widetilde\operatorname{ch}^{\wedge}_{T,\alpha_j,u}}V\\
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(Y_i,\alpha_i)
 @>{\Phi^H_{\tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(L_{ij})}}>>
 \widehat H^k_{T,\operatorname{del},\operatorname{per}}(Y_j,\alpha_j)
\end{CD}
\end{equation}
is commutative.

\item For composable kernels with proper convolution support, put
\[
 Z_{02}^{\star}:=
 \mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{02}\bigl(\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{01}^{-1}Z_{01}\cap\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{12}^{-1}Z_{12}\bigr)\subset W_{02}.
\]
For connected outer inertia components $\mathcal F_0\subset IY_0$ and
$\mathcal F_2\subset IY_2$, set
\[
 Z_{02}^{\star,\mathcal F_0,\mathcal F_2}
 :=IZ_{02}^{\star}\cap(\mathcal F_0\times\mathcal F_2).
\]
Then the following is an equality in the completed supported cohomology group of the ordinary outer product with the displayed common support:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:RR-convolution}
 \tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(L_{12}\star_{\operatorname{KU}}L_{01})
 =\tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(L_{12})\star_H
  \tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(L_{01})
\end{equation}
inside
\[
 \widehat H^0_{T,Z_{02}^{\star,\mathcal F_0,\mathcal F_2},\operatorname{per}}
 \bigl(\mathcal F_0\times\mathcal F_2;
 \mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_0^*\mathscr L_0^\vee\otimes\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_2^*\mathscr L_2\bigr)
\]
for every pair $(\mathcal F_0,\mathcal F_2)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Use $K=S^1$ and the finite free spaces $E_N$. At the $N$-th Borel approximation, the ambient product is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Borel-ambient-product}
 E_N\times_K(Y_i\times Y_j) \simeq (Y_i)_N\times_{B_N}(Y_j)_N.
\end{equation}
Its projection to $(Y_j)_N$ has vertical tangent bundle equal to the pullback of $TY_i$ and, on the fixed sector $\mathcal F_i$, relative complex dimension $d_i$. The support condition $Z_{ij}\subset Y_i\times_\mathbb A Y_j$ changes neither statement. This is where the ambient-product convention is essential.

Choose an integer $s$ annihilating the finite-order twisting classes $\alpha_i$ and represent all of them by banded $\mu_s$-gerbes; then use the central-weight idempotents. The trace of a source-inverse/target-positive kernel has coefficient line $\mathscr L_i^\vee\otimes\mathscr L_j$; weights and middle coefficient lines cancel under tensor product by fusion. Apply the Atiyah--Singer families theorem~\cite{ASFamilies} and the finite-group fixed-point and stack Riemann--Roch formulas~\cite{ASIndex}, \cite{KawasakiRR}, \cite{ToenRR}, \cite{EdidinDMRR} to the supported projection in \eqref{eq:Borel-ambient-product}. The fixed-point ratio of source and target moving-normal factors is precisely $\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_i^*\widetilde\operatorname{Td}_T(TY_i)$; the target factor cancels. The family index lowers ordinary degree by $2d_i$, so periodization gives the factor $u^{d_i}$. This proves the finite-approximation version of \eqref{eq:RR-square} in even parity. Odd parity follows by external product with the suspension generator; pullback, multiplication by the even kernel, trace projectors, and supported pushforward commute with suspension.

Apply the same index formula to the supported middle projection on 
$Y_0\times Y_1\times Y_2$. At every finite stage, it gives the equality of supported kernel classes corresponding to \eqref{eq:RR-convolution}. The relative tangent bundle of that middle projection is the pullback of $TY_1$, so the factor is $u^{d_1}$ and
the middle inertial Todd class is exactly the one in the cohomological convolution. Functoriality of the family index, the projection formula, and associativity of fusion give the convolution identity.

Finally pass to the inverse limit. Theorem~\ref{thm:general-completed-ch} controls the state-space towers, while Theorem~\ref{thm:supported-completion} controls the relative-pair towers containing the supported kernel classes. Both are Mittag--Leffler and have no $\varprojlim^1$ term. Thus the finite-stage operator square and, separately, the finite-stage equality of supported classes pass to the completed limits.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
The theorem is unrigidified and additive. It does not construct any of the kernels, identify a Chow cycle with a virtual structure sheaf, or eliminate nonidentity Kawasaki sectors. Rigidified orbifold Gromov--Witten classes enter only after the canonical descent of Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-rigidification-descent}, the
stack-normalized transport \eqref{eq:transport-rigid-to-del}, and an independently constructed coefficient-valued reduced orbifold theory.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
\label{thm:cohomological-95}
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)}]
\item an independently constructed standard rigidified twisted reduced orbifold theory whose coefficient-valued virtual class and two-point operator are compatible with the canonical descended transgression lines of 
Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-rigidification-descent} and with the fusion, inversion, and unit coherences;

\item an ambient-product coefficient-valued kernel $\Xi_P$ from $X$ to $\widehat X$, supported in $X\times_\mathbb A\widehat X$, whose transform is an isomorphism and satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cohomological-GS-reduction}
 \Phi^H_{\Xi_P}\bmod z=\Phi^H_{\operatorname{GS}};
\end{equation}

\item the independently defined enumerative kernels $\Xi^X_\beta$ and 
$\Xi^{\widehat X,\operatorname{del}}_{\bar\beta}$; and

\item the ambient-product supported identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cohomological-global-convolution}
 \Xi_P\star_H\Xi^X_\beta=\Xi^{\widehat X,\operatorname{del}}_{\bar\beta}\star_H\Xi_P.
\end{equation}
Writing $Z_P^H$, $Z_X^H$, and $Z_{\widehat X}^H$ for the supports of the three cohomological kernels, define $Z_L^H$ and $Z_R^H$ to be the proper outer images of, respectively,
\[
 \mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{01}^{-1}Z_X^H\cap\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{12}^{-1}Z_P^H,
 \qquad
 \mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{01}^{-1}Z_P^H\cap\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{12}^{-1}Z_{\widehat X}^H.
\]
For every connected outer component $\mathcal F\subset I\widehat X$, identity \eqref{eq:cohomological-global-convolution} is required in
\[
 \widehat H^0_{T,(Z_L^H\cup Z_R^H)\cap(X\times\mathcal F),\operatorname{per}}
 \bigl(X\times\mathcal F;\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{\mathcal F}^*\mathscr L_{\alpha,\mathcal F}\bigr),
\]
after the canonical extension-of-support maps of Definition~\ref{def:common-support}.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:del-intertwining}
 F^{\widehat X,\operatorname{del}}_{\bar\beta}\Phi^H_{\Xi_P}=\Phi^H_{\Xi_P}F^X_\beta.
\end{equation}
The horizontal map to the standard rigidified Chen--Ruan-periodized state space is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:CR-horizontal}
 \Phi_P^{\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}:=\mathsf J^{-1}\mathsf S_{\mathrm{age}}^{-1}\Phi^H_{\Xi_P},
\end{equation}
and it satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:CR-intertwining}
 F^{\widehat X,\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}_{\bar\beta}\Phi_P^{\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}=\Phi_P^{\operatorname{rig},\operatorname{CR}}F^X_\beta.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Proposition~\ref{prop:H-convolution} converts
\eqref{eq:cohomological-global-convolution} into \eqref{eq:del-intertwining}.  Conjugate this identity by $\mathsf J^{-1}\mathsf S_{\mathrm{age}}^{-1}$ and use
\eqref{eq:PGL-del-operator}; the adjacent regrading and rigidification maps cancel and give \eqref{eq:CR-intertwining}. Condition \eqref{eq:cohomological-GS-reduction} identifies the nonequivariant reduction of the horizontal map with the chosen Groechenig--Shen map. Without that condition the theorem would concern an unspecified
integral transform.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
\label{rem:independent-C4}
Condition \textup{(C1)} should be a straightforward adaptation of the work of \cite{PRY}. Condition \textup{(C4)} is not a consequence of 
Theorem~\ref{thm:block-decomposition} or of the definition of convolution. Character decomposition only says that each operator is block diagonal. Even when $\Gamma$ is trivial, take a one-dimensional state space, $F_X=0$, $F_{\widehat X}=\operatorname{id}$ and $\Phi=\operatorname{id}$. All equivariance requirements hold, but $F_{\widehat X}\Phi\ne\Phi F_X$.  This elementary example disproves the asserted formal implication; it is not a counterexample to an enumerative comparison for Higgs moduli. A geometric proof of
\eqref{eq:cohomological-global-convolution} is additional work.
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
\label{thm:corrected-95}
Assume the following stronger data.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)}]
\item The independently constructed twisted reduced orbifold theory of \textup{(C1)}, including its fusion-compatible coefficient-valued virtual class and standard rigidified two-point operator.

\item A global ambient-product supported kernel
\[
 P\in\operatorname{KU}^0_{T,Z_P}(X\times\widehat X,\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{\widehat X}^*\alpha_T),
 \qquad Z_P\subset X\times_{\mathbb{A}}\widehat X,
\]
whose transform is an isomorphism and whose kernel-induced map of $\operatorname{KU}$-module spectra satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:P-recovers-GS}
 \mbox{For}_T(\Phi_P^{\operatorname{KU}})=\Phi_{\operatorname{GS}}^{\operatorname{KU}}
\end{equation}
after forgetting the $T$-action. $\mbox{For}_T(-)$. If only the weaker equality modulo
$z$ is known, replace \eqref{eq:P-recovers-GS} by $\Phi_P^H\bmod z=\Phi_{\operatorname{GS}}^H$ and call the result only a cohomological lift. If $P$ is called a Fourier equivalence, assume a type-correct convolution inverse $Q$.

\item Ambient-product supported kernels
\begin{align*}
 K_{X,\beta}&\in\operatorname{KU}^0_{T,Z_X}(X\times X),
 &Z_X&\subset X\times_{\mathbb{A}} X,\\
 K_{\widehat X,\bar\beta}&\in
 \operatorname{KU}^0_{T,Z_{\widehat X}}
 (\widehat X\times\widehat X,
 \mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_1^*\alpha_T^{-1}\otimes\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_2^*\alpha_T),
 &Z_{\widehat X}&\subset\widehat X\times_{\mathbb{A}}\widehat X,
\end{align*}
with proper convolution supports. All three original support pairs, including the support pair of $P$, have finite equivariant CW type. Moreover, for every convolution in \textup{(H5)} and for every inverse convolution involving $Q$ when present, the relative pair defined on the ordinary triple product by the pulled-back intersection
\[
 \mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{01}^{-1}Z_{01}\cap\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{12}^{-1}Z_{12}
\]
and the relative pair defined by its proper image in the ordinary outer product both have finite equivariant CW type. The same requirement is imposed on every support pair used to represent the resulting convolution class and on every finite union of outer supports used as a common support in Definition~\ref{def:common-support}.

\item Their completed ambient-product Riemann--Roch classes are the independently defined enumerative kernels:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:RR-enumerative-identification}
 \tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(K_{X,\beta})=\Xi^X_\beta,
 \qquad
 \tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(K_{\widehat X,\bar\beta})=\Xi^{\widehat X,\operatorname{del}}_{\bar\beta}.
\end{equation}

\item Define the two proper outer supports in $X\times\widehat X$ by
\begin{align*}
 Z_L^{\operatorname{KU}}
 &:={\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits}_{02}\bigl({\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits}_{01}^{-1}Z_X
       \cap {\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits}_{12}^{-1}Z_P\bigr)
 &&\text{on }X\times X\times\widehat X,\\
 Z_R^{\operatorname{KU}}
 &:={\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits}_{02}\bigl({\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits}_{01}^{-1}Z_P
       \cap {\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits}_{12}^{-1}Z_{\widehat X}\bigr)
 &&\text{on }X\times\widehat X\times\widehat X.
\end{align*}
The ambient-product supported $K$-kernel identity is required after extension of supports in the explicit common group
\begin{equation}\label{eq:missing-global-convolution}
 P\star_{\operatorname{KU}}K_{X,\beta}=K_{\widehat X,\bar\beta}\star_{\operatorname{KU}}P
 \quad\text{in }
 \operatorname{KU}^0_{T,Z_L^{\operatorname{KU}}\cup Z_R^{\operatorname{KU}}}(X\times\widehat X,\mathop{\rm pr}\nolimits_{\widehat X}^*\alpha_T).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Then all hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:cohomological-95} hold, and its intertwining conclusions follow.
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Proposition~\ref{prop:K-convolution} turns \eqref{eq:missing-global-convolution} into the corresponding equality of completed $K$-theory operators. Theorem~\ref{thm:bivariant-RR}, whose kernel-level passage to completion is justified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:supported-completion}, sends the $K$-kernel identity (\ref{eq:missing-global-convolution}) to
\[
 \tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(P)\star_H\Xi^X_\beta 
 =\Xi^{\widehat X,\operatorname{del}}_{\bar\beta}\star_H\tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(P).
\]
Put $\Xi_P=\tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(P)$. The general completed Chern-character square shows that its transform is an isomorphism. Forgetting the $T$-action in \eqref{eq:P-recovers-GS}, or merely reducing modulo $z$ in the weaker version, gives
\eqref{eq:cohomological-GS-reduction}. Thus Theorem~\ref{thm:cohomological-95} applies.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{cor:genuine-kernel-transport}
Suppose $P$ satisfies \textup{(H2)}, has convolution inverse $Q$, and all support and finite-type hypotheses needed below hold. Then
\[
K_{\widehat X,\bar\beta}^{\operatorname{FM}}:=P\star_{\operatorname{KU}}K_{X,\beta}\star_{\operatorname{KU}}Q
\]
is its transported kernel. Identifying the transported cohomological operator with the independently constructed enumerative operator still requires, for example, the separate supported equality
\begin{equation}\label{eq:transport-enumerative-test}
 \tau^{T,\operatorname{orb}}(K_{\widehat X,\bar\beta}^{\operatorname{FM}})=\Xi^{\widehat X,\operatorname{del}}_{\bar\beta}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Convolution with $P$ and $Q$ gives the transported kernel by
Proposition~\ref{prop:K-convolution}; the Riemann--Roch square in Theorem \ref{thm:bivariant-RR} gives its cohomological action. That action is the enumerative one if \eqref{eq:transport-enumerative-test} holds. The supported Chern character, followed by the invertible relative Todd factor, is an isomorphism only after complexification and completion under the hypotheses used here.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:full-divisor-comparison}
Suppose an isomorphism $\Phi$, independent of the Novikov variables, intertwines all reduced positive-degree two-point operators. Suppose also that a chosen correspondence of curve degrees and divisors matches the Novikov monomials and divisor pairings, and that
\[
 \Phi(D_T\cup-)= (\widehat D_T\cup_{\operatorname{CR}}-)\Phi.
\]
Then, over a common Novikov completion, $\Phi M_D=M_{\widehat D}\Phi$.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Use the divisor formulas on both sides. The hypothesis matches the degree-zero terms.  The curve-degree convention, divisor pairing and coefficientwise intertwining match every positive-degree term. Completeness permits their sum. This proves the operator assertion stated.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:smooth-vanishing}
For every nonzero effective curve class, the reduced two-pointed stable-map
correspondences of $X$ and of $\widehat X$ restrict to $0$ over $\mathbb A^{\mathrm{sm}}$.  Hence every positive-degree square in Theorem~\ref{thm:corrected-95} commutes after restriction to that locus, with both vertical maps zero.
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
A smooth fixed-determinant Hitchin fiber is a torsor under an Prym variety. After choosing a point, it becomes an abelian variety, and every morphism from $\mathbb P^1$ to it is constant: pulling back the translation-invariant one-forms shows that its differential vanishes Each irreducible component of a connected genus-zero nodal source is therefore mapped constantly, and connectedness forces the entire map to be constant.

For the quotient $\widehat{X}$, the finite group acts fiberwise by translations. The
coarse quotient of an abelian torsor by a finite translation subgroup is again a torsor under an abelian variety. The coarse map of a twisted genus-zero stable map to $\widehat{X}$ is therefore constant over $\mathbb A^{\mathrm{sm}}$. A map contained in a residual finite gerbe may carry orbifold monodromy, but its coarse curve class is $0$.  Thus no positive-degree stable map occurs on either side, proving the assertion.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:hitchin-constant}
Let \(D\) be a connected proper nodal curve and let 
\(f:D\to X\) be a
morphism.  Then
\[
 h\circ f:D\longrightarrow\mathbb A
\]
is constant.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
The variety \(\mathbb A\) is affine.  Since \(D\) is connected and proper, $H^0(D,\mathcal O_D)=\mathbb C$. Every coordinate function on the affine space \(\mathbb A\) hence pulls back to a constant function on \(D\), so \(h\circ f\) is constant.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:stablemap-proper}
For every \(\beta\) and \(n\), the morphism $\rho_{\beta}$ is proper. For \(n\ge1\), every evaluation morphism
\[
 \operatorname{ev}:\overline M_{0,n}(X,\beta)\longrightarrow X^n_\mathbb A
\]
is proper.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
By Theorem \ref{thm:hitchin-proper}, \(X\to\mathbb A\) is projective. Choose an \(h\)-ample line bundle \(H\) and put 
\(e=H\cdot\beta\). The stack of stable maps to the fibers of \(h\), with fixed genus, number of markings, and \(H\)-degree \(e\), is a finite-type proper stack over \(\mathbb A\); this is the relative form of the standard properness theorem
for stable maps, see \cite{BM} and \cite{FP}. In a connected family of stable maps, the pushforward fundamental class
\((f_s)_*[\mathcal C_s]\in H_2(X,{\mathbb Z})\) is locally constant; equivalently, the moduli stack decomposes into open-and-closed substacks indexed by the integral curve class. Consequently, the locus of class \(\beta\) is open and closed in this finite-type stack. It is a finite union of connected components and is therefore proper over \(\mathbb A\). This also
proves that \(\overline M_{0,n}(X,\beta)\) is of finite type.

For the evaluation map, write ${\mathcal M}=\overline M_{0,n}(X,\beta), Y=X_\mathbb A^n$. The morphism \({\mathcal M}\to\mathbb A\) is proper and \(Y\to\mathbb A\) is separated. The graph $\Gamma_{\operatorname{ev}}\hookrightarrow{\mathcal M}\times_\mathbb A Y$ is therefore closed. The projection ${\mathcal M}\times_\mathbb A Y\longrightarrow Y$ is the base change of the proper morphism \({\mathcal M}\to\mathbb A\), hence is proper.
Thus
\[
 \text{ev}: {\mathcal M}\xrightarrow{\,\Gamma_{\operatorname{ev}}\,}{\mathcal M}\times_\mathbb A Y\longrightarrow Y
\]
is proper.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{cor:fixed-proper}
For every \(\beta\) and \(n\), $\overline M_{0,n}(X,\beta)^T$ is proper.
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
A \(T\)-fixed stable map has \(T\)-fixed Hitchin value. Since $\mathbb A^{T}=\{0\}$, this value is \(0\). Therefore
\[
 \overline M_{0,n}(X,\beta)^T \subset \rho_\beta^{-1}(0).
\]
The fiber \(\rho_\beta^{-1}(0)\) is proper by Proposition \ref{prop:stablemap-proper}, and the fixed locus is closed in it.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:semireg-surj}
If \(\beta\ne0\), the cosection \eqref{eq:semireg-ob} is everywhere surjective.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
At a stable map \(f:D\to X\), the relative obstruction map is
\[
 H^1(D,f^*T_X)\longrightarrow H^1(D,\omega_D)\otimes\mathbb C_1\cong\mathbb C_1.
\]
Its Serre dual sends the generator of \(H^0(D,\mathcal O_D)\) to the section obtained from \(df\) by the nondegenerate pairing \(\omega\). Since \(\beta\ne0\), the map is nonconstant on some irreducible component. In characteristic zero, \(df\) is nonzero at the generic point of that component. The dual map from a one-dimensional vector space is therefore
injective, so the displayed obstruction map is surjective. By \cite[Proposition~6.4]{KL}, the absolute and relative cosections have the same degeneracy locus. Hence \(\sigma_\omega\) is everywhere surjective. Equivalently, Kiem--Li's degeneracy locus consists of \(\omega\)-null maps; nondegeneracy of \(\omega\) makes such a map constant.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:kernel-cone-general}
Let \(M\) be a finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack with a \(T\)-equivariant perfect obstruction theory
\(E^\bullet\to L_M\) of virtual dimension \(v\). Let \(\mathcal L\) be a \(T\)-equivariant line bundle and suppose that there is a surjection
\[
 \sigma:\operatorname{Ob}_M=h^1\bigl((E^\bullet)^\vee\bigr)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L.
\]
Then \(\sigma\) canonically induces a morphism of vector-bundle stacks
\[
 \widetilde\sigma: \mathfrak E:=h^1/h^0\bigl((E^\bullet)^\vee\bigr) \longrightarrow\mathbb V(\mathcal L).
\]
Here \(\mathbb V(\mathcal L)=\operatorname{Spec}_M\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal L^\vee)\) is the total-space vector bundle. Its kernel \(\mathfrak K\) is a vector-bundle stack of virtual rank \(-v-1\). The intrinsic-normal-cone cycle is supported in that kernel,
\[
 [\mathfrak C_M]\in Z_*^T(\mathfrak K).
\]
Writing \(\pi_{\mathfrak K}:\mathfrak K\to M\), homotopy invariance gives
\[
 \pi_{\mathfrak K}^*:A_j^T(M)_{{\mathbb Q}} \xrightarrow{\,\sim\,}A_{j-v-1}^T(\mathfrak K)_{\mathbb Q}.
\]
Consequently, \(0^!_{\mathfrak K}:=(\pi_{\mathfrak K}^*)^{-1}\) is the presentation-independent zero-section Gysin map, and the class
\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-kernel-class}
 [M]^{\mathrm{ker}}_T :=0^!_{\mathfrak K}[\mathfrak C_M] \in A_{v+1}^T(M)_{\mathbb Q}
\end{equation}
satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-excess}
 [M]^{\mathrm{vir}}_T =c_1^T(\mathcal L)\cap[M]^{\mathrm{ker}}_T.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Behrend--Fantechi construct \(h^1/h^0\) intrinsically and functorially from the derived object; see \cite[Propositions~2.4 and~2.5]{BF}. In the derived category, the canonical truncation followed by the cosection,
\[
 (E^\bullet)^\vee
 \longrightarrow h^1\bigl((E^\bullet)^\vee\bigr)[-1]
 \xrightarrow{\ \sigma[-1]\ }\mathcal L[-1],
\]
induces \(\widetilde\sigma\). Work first nonequivariantly and choose, \'etale locally on \(M\), a two-term vector-bundle presentation
\[
 (E^\bullet)^\vee=[E_0\xrightarrow{d}E_1] \quad\text{in degrees }[0,1].
\]
The composite
\[
 E_1\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(d)
 =\operatorname{Ob}_M\xrightarrow{\sigma}\mathcal L
\]
is surjective and annihilates \(d(E_0)\). If \(F_1\) is its kernel, then \(F_1\) is a vector bundle and the required morphism and its kernel have the local presentations
\[
 \widetilde\sigma:[E_1/E_0]\longrightarrow\mathbb V(\mathcal L),
 \qquad
 \mathfrak K=[F_1/E_0].
\]
On overlaps, quasi-isomorphisms between two presentations induce the canonical equivalence of their \(h^1/h^0\) stacks and commute with the map to \(\mathcal L\), because both maps induce the fixed sheaf morphism \(\sigma\). Thus the kernels and their zero sections satisfy descent and define the global vector-bundle stack \(\mathfrak K\), of virtual rank \((\mathop{\rm rk} F_1)-\mathop{\rm rk} E_0=-v-1\). Finite-type Deligne--Mumford stacks admit stratifications by global quotients
\cite[Proposition~4.5.5(iii)]{Kresch}. Hence homotopy invariance for vector-bundle stacks 
\cite[Proposition~5.3.2]{Kresch} applies to \(\pi_{\mathfrak K}:\mathfrak K\to M\), and shows directly that
\(0^!_{\mathfrak K}=(\pi_{\mathfrak K}^*)^{-1}\) is intrinsic and independent of every local two-term presentation.  For the standard obstruction stack \(\mathfrak E\), this inverse-pullback construction recovers the Behrend--Fantechi virtual class: independence from a chosen global resolution is \cite[Proposition~5.3]{BF}, and Kresch's
\cite[Theorem~6.2.1]{Kresch} removes the global-resolution hypothesis.

After trivializing \(\mathcal L\), Kiem--Li's cone-reduction theorem \cite[Proposition~4.3]{KL} places the intrinsic-cone cycle, with its multiplicities, in \([F_1/E_0]\). Multiplying a trivialization of \(\mathcal L\) by a unit changes neither the kernel nor that cycle, so these local statements descend and give \([\mathfrak C_M]\in Z_*(\mathfrak K)\). This proves that \eqref{eq:abstract-kernel-class} is globally defined.


The excess identity can be proved globally, without assuming that rational Chow identities descend from an \'etale cover. The map $\mathfrak E\to\mathbb V(\mathcal L)$ is locally a surjective linear map. Its zero locus 
$i:\mathfrak K\hookrightarrow\mathfrak E$ is therefore a regular codimension-one embedding with normal line
$\pi_{\mathfrak K}^*\mathcal L$. For $a\in A_*(M)$, flat base change along the vector-bundle-stack projection gives
\[
 i_*\pi_{\mathfrak K}^*a =\pi_{\mathfrak E}^*\bigl(c_1(\mathcal L)\cap a\bigr).
\]
One may also obtain this equality from the zero-section self-intersection formula for $\mathcal L$ and homotopy invariance. These are global Chow operations. Writing $B=\pi_{\mathfrak K}^*a$ and applying the inverse of $\pi_{\mathfrak E}^*$ proves
\[
 0^!_{\mathfrak E}i_*B =c_1(\mathcal L)\cap0^!_{\mathfrak K}B.
\]

Taking
\(B=[\mathfrak C_M]\) proves \eqref{eq:abstract-excess}. Finally, apply the entire construction to the Borel approximations. The descended obstruction sheaf and line bundle are \((\operatorname{Ob}_M\times U)/T\) and
\((\mathcal L\times U)/T\); intrinsic cones, Chern classes, and zero-section Gysin maps commute with the smooth transition maps between good pairs. The compatible ordinary identities therefore stabilize to the stated equivariant Chow identities and prove equivariant presentation independence.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
\label{rem:kernel-caveat}
Everywhere surjectivity is essential in Proposition \ref{prop:kernel-cone-general}. With a nonempty degeneracy locus the kernel cone need not be a vector-bundle stack globally, and one must instead use Kiem--Li's localized Gysin map.  Moreover, the proposition asserts cycle-theoretic support of \([\mathfrak C_M]\) in \(\mathfrak K\); it does not assert a stronger scheme-theoretic factorization of the entire cone or construct a reduced perfect obstruction theory.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
